# SQQ {#sqq}

SQQ 0.5.8 counts shortest-path chordless rings of size 4, 5 and 6.
d-SEAMS counts primitive rings, and that census includes
3-rings, which SQQ does not search. On a crystal the two censuses
are the same list. On a disordered hydrogen-bond network they are
not, and an ice label that reads those rings moves with them.

The ice comparison has three readings. The merged label puts
published CHILL+, which does not search rings, next to SQQ’s ice
stage on chordless 6-rings. The primitive reading applies that same
SQQ ice rule to the d-SEAMS primitive 6-rings. The chordless reading
applies it to the d-SEAMS chordless 6-rings. The chordless reading
is the like-for-like label. The merged reading is the whole-tool
label.

## The 4096-molecule TIP4P/2005 frame {#the-4096-molecule-tip4p-2005-frame}

The oxygen-oxygen edges and the rings match.

| quantity | d-SEAMS | SQQ | agreement |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| O-O edges | 10495 | 10495 | 1 |
| 4-rings | 1758 | 1758 | 1 |
| 5-rings | 2763 | 2763 | 1 |
| 6-rings | 2485 | 2485 | 1 |
| chordless 6-rings | 4045 | 4045 | 1 |

The merged ice label does not. Published CHILL+ names 4 molecules
ice and SQQ names 1129. The agreement is 0.724854. The SQQ rule on
the primitive 6-rings names 1075, agreement 0.986816 against SQQ’s

1. The same rule on the chordless 6-rings names 1129 on both

sides, agreement 1, all 4096 molecules.

The ring lists already match, so the merged gap is the choice of
ice rule. CHILL+ reads four bond correlations. SQQ reads the
chordless 6-rings. Once both sides use the chordless rings, the
labels agree.

Eight repeats, mean milliseconds. The ratio is SQQ divided by d-SEAMS.

| operation | threads | d-SEAMS | SQQ | ratio |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rings | 1 | 22.6026 | 1054.3846 | 46.649 |
| rings | 8 | 8.2165 | 1056.0863 | 128.532 |
| ice, CHILL+ against SQQ | 1 | 1.7860 | 914.2565 | 511.905 |
| ice, CHILL+ against SQQ | 8 | 1.5802 | 916.2551 | 579.849 |
| ice, chordless rings | 1 | 28.5570 | 914.2565 | 32.015 |
| ice, chordless rings | 8 | 7.9694 | 916.2551 | 114.971 |

SQQ is one Python process. Extra threads do not shorten it. The
d-SEAMS ring search does shorten, so the ratio rises from one
thread to eight.

## Where else the lists agree {#where-else-the-lists-agree}

Ideal ice Ic and ice Ih, at 4096 and at 110592 molecules, match on
the edges, the 4-rings, the 5-rings, the 6-rings, the chordless
6-rings and every ice reading. Each crystal has two 6-rings per
molecule and no 4-ring or 5-ring.

The 4096-molecule mW liquid matches on the edges and the rings.
Its merged ice agreement is 0.561768 (81 against 1851). The
chordless reading matches, 1851 on both sides.

The 250-molecule TIP4P oxygen frame matches on the edges and the
rings. Its merged ice agreement is 0.176000 (0 against 206). The
chordless reading matches, 206 on both sides.

The 110592-molecule mW liquid is the frame that misses. The
oxygen-oxygen edges are 259187 and 259186. The 4-rings are 34097
and 34098, the 5-rings 86218 and 86217, the 6-rings 85092 and
85094, and the chordless 6-rings 123915 and 123917. The chordless
ice reading is 50120 against 50121, agreement 0.999991. The merged
ice agreement is 0.561957.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/stacking-disorder.md -->

# Stacking disorder {#stacking-disorder}

Cubic ice and hexagonal ice are the same puckered hexagons stacked in
two orders. Hexagonal ice repeats every two layers. Cubic ice repeats
every three, and the next layer sits over the hole of the one before.
A stacking fault is one layer in the other order. Both crystals, and
the fault between them, have a high local $q_6$. A cutoff on $q_6$
therefore reports ice and stops.

Two counts in this tree keep the polytypes apart.

The cage census names the cages. A hexagonal layer is a six-ring that
is the base of a hexagonal cage: two basal faces and three prismatic
faces. A cubic layer is a six-ring that closes a double-diamond cage.
A molecule that belongs to both cages is `both`. The rest of each cage
is `hexagonal` or `cubic`. None of those names is a threshold on
$q_6$. `seams cages` prints the four counts.

```bash
seams cages input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1
```

On that 864-molecule slab the seeded graph and the cutoff graph both
print hexagonal 444, cubic 0, `both` 0 and water 420. The mutual graph
prints hexagonal 442, cubic 0, `both` 0 and water 422. The one cubic molecule in the slab is not a
double-diamond cage, and no molecule sits in both cages.

CHILL+ names hexagonal and cubic from the bond correlations, and
`--layers` writes the stack along the long edge. The published rule is
the 2015 table. The account of that rule is
[CHILL+: the published rule and the OVITO rule](chill-plus-rules.md).

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/interface_f0.lammpstrj --type 1 --layers --axis 2
```

The frame is the one in
[the interface tutorial](../user/tutorials/interface.md).
The command prints hexagonal 352, cubic 1 and water 434, and the stack
`HHHHHHHH....C.`: eight hexagonal slabs, a gap, and one cubic layer.
A $q_6$ cutoff would add the 352 and the 1. The stack string keeps
them apart, which is what a growth rate on the basal face needs. The
front advances by a layer of one polytype. The fault is that layer.

The same split is why a nucleation frame reports cubic and hexagonal
counts separately. On `input/traj/nucleation_f1.lammpstrj` the published
rule prints hexagonal 62 and cubic 47. The largest crystal cluster can
contain both, and the fraction of each says which polytype the nucleus
is growing. $q_6$ on that cluster is one number.


---

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/symmetry.md -->

# Local symmetry {#local-symmetry}

The classifier names each oxygen as ice Ih, ice Ic, stacking-disordered
ice, or unmatched, and it can name a hydrate cage or a five- or six-ring
when one cluster is passed in. The per-atom ice label is the production
path. The command and the per-atom call are on
[the symmetry classifier](../user/howto/symmetry-classifier.md).

A crystal oxygen is ice Ih (0), ice Ic (1), or stacking-disordered ice
(2). Anything else is -1. The seventeen-atom shell is the central
oxygen, its four nearest neighbours, and the twelve neighbours of those
four. That is the shell polyhedral template matching uses for diamond
(Larsen, Schmidt and Schiøtz, *Modelling and Simulation in Materials Science and Engineering* 24, 055007, 2016,
DOI 10.1088/0965-0393/24/5/055007,
[arXiv:1603.05143](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.05143)).

## Neighbours {#neighbours}

The bond cutoff is 3.5 Å. A neighbour closer than 2.15 Å is dropped.
The four nearest bonds are kept. One thread walks each pair once, using
half of the 27-cell stencil, and writes both ends of the bond. Several
threads scan the full stencil and write one end. When the cell is
orthorhombic and every edge is at least three bond lengths, the atoms
are wrapped into the box and histogrammed into cells of that cutoff.
A skewed cell uses a wider stencil. The coordinate columns are reused
on the next frame of the same size.

A center whose four bonds do not all lie between 2.30 Å and 3.35 Å is
left unmatched, and the second shell is not read.

## Tetrahedral order {#tetrahedral-order}

The tetrahedral order parameter $q$ is the Chau–Hardwick /
Errington–Debenedetti invariant of the four bonds (Errington and
Debenedetti, *Nature* 409, 318, 2001,
[10.1038/35053024](https://doi.org/10.1038/35053024)). With
$\theta_{jk}$ the angle at the center between neighbours $j$ and
$k$,

$$
q = 1 - \frac{3}{8}
\sum_{j=1}^{3} \sum_{k=j+1}^{4}
\left(\cos\theta_{jk} + \frac{1}{3}\right)^{2}.
$$

Equal bonds skip this test. An ideal crystal has equal bonds, and the
staggered test below names it. Otherwise a center with $q < 0.85$ is
left unmatched and the second shell is not read. The library constant
is `kThermalQ`.

## Common-neighbour fingerprint {#common-neighbour-fingerprint}

The second shell is the adaptive-cutoff common-neighbour signature of
Maras, Trushin, Stukowski, Albe and Nordlund, *Computer Physics Communications* 205, 13 (2016), Appendix A
([10.1016/j.cpc.2016.04.001](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpc.2016.04.001)).
The cutoff for a bond of length $r$ is $r(1+\sqrt{2})/2$.

Twelve $(4,2,1)$ patterns are ice Ic. Six $(4,2,1)$ and six
$(4,2,2)$ are ice Ih. A partial cubic signature needs at least eight
good patterns, at least as many $(4,2,1)$ as $(4,2,2)$, at least
eight $(4,2,1)$, and $q \ge 0.97$. Six or seven $(4,2,1)$
patterns are not labeled cubic. With $q \ge 0.97$ they are passed
to the fit. Below that, the fit runs only when the conditions in the
next section hold. A partial
hexagonal signature needs at least eight good patterns, more
$(4,2,2)$ than $(4,2,1)$, at least four $(4,2,2)$, and the same
$q \ge 0.97$.

A second shell whose radii differ by more than a factor 1.45 does not
receive this signature. It can still be fitted when $q \ge 0.85$, the
longest of the four bonds is at most 1.20 times the shortest, and the
second-shell radii differ by at most a factor 1.6.

An ideal shell, equal bonds and one second-shell radius, is named from
the raw cosine of each second-shell bond with another first-shell bond
and does not build this signature. The bond vectors are not projected.
On the ideal cell that cosine is $1/3$ for a staggered arm and $7/9$
for an eclipsed arm. The fast path compares the squares, $1/9$ and
$49/81$. An arm is eclipsed when the best square is at least 0.36,
and staggered when that square is at most 0.25. Four staggered arms are
ice Ic. One eclipsed arm and three staggered arms are ice Ih.

## The fit {#the-fit}

A shell is fitted when the fingerprint did not name it, it already has
one crystal neighbour, $q \ge 0.85$, the longest bond is at most 1.20
times the shortest, and the second-shell radius varies by at most a
factor 1.6. Both clouds are centered. The optimal rotation is a
quaternion (Horn, *Journal of the Optical Society of America A* 4, 629,
1987, [10.1364/JOSAA.4.000629](https://doi.org/10.1364/JOSAA.4.000629);
Coutsias, Seok and Dill, *Journal of Computational Chemistry* 25, 1849,
2004, [10.1002/jcc.20110](https://doi.org/10.1002/jcc.20110)). The
residual is the root-mean-square distance after that rotation, divided
by the template radius, the normalization Larsen, Schmidt and Schiøtz
use. Zero is a perfect shape. The ceiling is `kShellRmsd`, 0.15:

$$
\frac{\mathrm{RMSD}}{R_{\mathrm{template}}} \le 0.15.
$$

`seams symmetry` uses that ceiling. A positive `shell_rmsd` on
`seams_system_symmetry` or `seams_symmetry_classify_tol` replaces it.
A non-positive value selects 0.15 again.

The bond-angle fingerprint names the one template the fit tries. This
cosine is the azimuthal one: both bonds are projected onto the plane
perpendicular to the central bond. Ideal staggered ice lies at 60
degrees, cosine $1/2$, and ideal eclipsed ice lies at 0 degrees,
cosine 1. An arm above 0.90 is eclipsed. Four eclipsed arms are left
unmatched, except on the recovery pass, where that pattern is
hexagonal. The eclipsed arm is anchored to the eclipsed arm of the
template. The four-point orientation uses one Jacobi sweep and the
seventeen-atom residual uses two. A shell that is still far after a few
correspondences is left unmatched, and a shell with only one crystal
neighbour is abandoned sooner than a shell with two.

After the labels are written, a crystal atom that has no crystal
neighbour among its four bonds is returned to unmatched. Hexagonal
recovery is one pass over the atoms left unmatched. It tries an atom
that already has three crystal neighbours, and on that pass four
eclipsed arms can be ice Ih.

## Cages, rings, and the other codes {#cages-rings-and-the-other-codes}

The same in-tree matcher names a cage or a ring. It is a 3×3 SVD with
the permutation fixed by the bond graph. The continuous shape measure
of that overlay is the scaled residual of Pinsky and Avnir (*Inorganic Chemistry* 37, 5575, 1998,
[10.1021/ic9804925](https://doi.org/10.1021/ic9804925)) and of the
Alvarez shape measure (*Coordination Chemistry Reviews* 249, 1693,
2005, [10.1016/j.ccr.2005.03.031](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ccr.2005.03.031)).

IRA (Gunde, Salles, Hémeryck and Martin-Samos, *Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling* 61, 5446, 2021,
[10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00567](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.1c00567))
is an optional second matcher for the same templates. SOFI, from the
same group (*Journal of Chemical Physics* 161, 062503, 2024,
[10.1063/5.0215689](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0215689)), names the
point group. spglib (Togo, Shinohara and Tanaka, *Science and Technology of Advanced Materials: Methods* 4, 2384822, 2024,
[10.1080/27660400.2024.2384822](https://doi.org/10.1080/27660400.2024.2384822))
names the space group. CHILL+ (Nguyen and Molinero, *Journal of Physical Chemistry B* 119, 9369, 2015,
[10.1021/jp510289t](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp510289t)) is a different
label. The two CHILL+ rules are on
[CHILL+: the published rule and the OVITO rule](chill-plus-rules.md).

A build uses IRA and SOFI when libira is linked, and spglib when
libsymspg is linked. Without libira the matcher is the in-tree Kabsch
search. `pointGroup` returns status 2 when SOFI is absent.
`spaceGroup` returns status 2 when spglib is absent, and
`seams symmetry` then prints `space-group off`.

## What the command prints {#what-the-command-prints}

`seams symmetry` prints the matcher, a space-group line, one shell
overlay when a crystal shell exists, and the tally. The names are
`ice-Ih`, `ice-Ic`, `ice-Isd`, and `unmatched`.

```bash
seams symmetry input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj --type 1
seams symmetry input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1
```

On the 128-molecule ice Ih cell the tally is `shells ice-Ih 128 unmatched 0`. On the 4096-molecule mW cubic cell it is `shells ice-Ic 4096 unmatched 0`. A build without libira reports `symmetry backend kabsch`.

The same call on the shipped frames, with this ceiling:

| frame | molecules | ice Ih | ice Ic | stacking-disordered | unmatched |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| interface_f0.lammpstrj | 864 | 245 | 0 | 0 | 619 |
| nucleation_f1.lammpstrj | 4096 | 8 | 12 | 1 | 4075 |

Published CHILL+ on those frames is a wider crystal. The interface slab
is hexagonal 352, cubic 1, interfacial 49, clathrate 3, interfacial
clathrate 25 and water 434. The nucleation frame is hexagonal 62, cubic
47, interfacial 240, clathrate 20, interfacial clathrate 138 and water

1. CHILL+ cubic and hexagonal need four bond correlations in the

staggered or eclipsed windows. The shell also asks for the
common-neighbour signature or a residual at most 0.15, and for a
crystal neighbour. CHILL+ has an interfacial label. The shell does not,
so two or three staggered bonds stay unmatched.

C++, in `symm`, `classifyIce` writes one label per row. The default
ceiling is `kShellRmsd` (0.15), the tetrahedral cutoff is `kThermalQ`
(0.85), and the bond-length ratio is `kThermalBondRatio` (1.20).
`classifyIceArrays` is the same call on three coordinate columns.
`best`, `matchKernel` and `matchAll` name one environment. The template
names are `ice-Ih`, `ice-Ic`, `ice-Isd`, `5^12`, `5^12 6^2`,
`5^12 6^4`, `ring-5` and `ring-6`.

C, in `seams_c_api.h`, `seams_symmetry_classify` writes the same labels
at the library ceiling. `seams_symmetry_classify_tol` takes an explicit
ceiling. `seams_symmetry_classify_gates` also takes the tetrahedral
cutoff and the bond-length ratio.

Python is `dseams.symmetry` in
[PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib).
The per-atom integers are the ones above.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/topological-network.md -->

# Topological network criteria {#topological-network-criteria}

These are the criteria the classifiers use.
Worked counts are in the
[rings](../user/tutorials/rings.md),
[bulk ice](../user/tutorials/bulk-ice.md),
[order parameter](../user/tutorials/order-parameters.md) and
[confined water](../user/tutorials/confined-water.md) tutorials.
The two CHILL+ rules are compared on
[CHILL+: the published rule and the OVITO rule](chill-plus-rules.md).

## Bond correlation {#bond-correlation}

CHILL and CHILL+ look at $l = 3$.
With $N_b(i)$ neighbours,

$$
q_{3m}(i) = \frac{1}{N_b(i)} \sum_{j \in N(i)} Y_{3m}(\hat r_{ij})
$$

$$
c_{ij} = \mathrm{Re}
\frac{\sum_m q_{3m}(i)\, q_{3m}(j)^{*}}
{\sqrt{\sum_m |q_{3m}(i)|^2 \sum_m |q_{3m}(j)|^2}}
$$

A bond is staggered when $c_{ij} \le -0.8$.
The eclipsed window is the part that differs:

| rule | eclipsed | staggered | neighbours |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CHILL | -0.2 \le c_{ij} \le -0.05 | c_{ij} \le -0.8 | 4 |
| CHILL+ | -0.35 \le c_{ij} \le 0.25 | c_{ij} \le -0.8 | 4 |

The code stores those edges as `chill::chillRule` `(-0.8, -0.2, -0.05, 4)` and `chill::chillPlusRule` `(-0.8, -0.35, 0.25, 4)`.
For those two rules the boundaries are inclusive.
`ovito-chill+` uses the CHILL+ numbers with open edges:
$c_{ij} < -0.8$ is staggered, and the eclipsed window is open at both ends.

The four-bond star is the phase.
Both published rules read the four nearest neighbours.
CHILL labels from that star even when a fifth oxygen lies inside the cutoff.
CHILL+ first requires the cutoff shell itself to hold exactly four neighbours, so that fifth oxygen is water.
The average in Nguyen and Molinero, equation 1 (J. Phys. Chem. B 2015, 119, 9369), is still over the four nearest,

$$
q_{lm}(i) = \frac{1}{4} \sum_{j=1}^{4} Y_{lm}(\hat r_{ij}).
$$

With four bonds the phases are:

| phase | eclipsed | staggered | further test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cubic | 0 | 4 |  |
| hexagonal | 1 | 3 |  |
| interfacial |  | 2 | a neighbour has more than two staggered bonds |
| interfacial | 0 | 3 | CHILL: a neighbour has exactly two staggered bonds. CHILL+: a neighbour has more than one |
| clathrate | 4 | 0 | CHILL+ only |
| interfacial clathrate | 3 |  | CHILL+ only |
| water |  |  | every remaining atom |

CHILL has no clathrate row.
An atom whose recorded bond count is not 4 is water under both rules.
`bop.hpp` lists the same phase names, and `chill::isInterfacial` is the neighbour test in the two interfacial rows.

`ovito-chill+` (`--rule ovito-chill+`, or the `ovito-chill+` command) is the OVITO 3.17.2 Chill+ modifier.
A crystal row still requires exactly four neighbours inside the cutoff.
$q_3$ is averaged over every neighbour in that shell, the edges are the open cuts above, and the interfacial rows do not consult a neighbour.
Two staggered bonds, or three staggered bonds and no eclipsed bond, are interfacial.

## Primitive rings {#primitive-rings}

A cycle is primitive, in the Franzblau sense, when for every pair of its vertices a shortest path in the bond graph lies along the cycle.
`primitive::ringNetwork` returns the primitive cycles whose size is at most `max_depth`.
The bond graph is an argument.
Mutual k-nearest, the union of those nominations, and a distance cutoff are three different graphs.
Quote the graph with the census.

## Cages {#cages}

A hexagonal cage is two basal six-rings and three prismatic six-rings.
A double-diamond cage is one equatorial six-ring and six peripheral rings.
`ring::cageAffiliation` evaluates those conditions for every six-ring.
`findHC` and `findDDC` claim rings as they accept them, so which rings they test depends on visiting order.
The affiliation predicates evaluate every six-ring.

The seeded variant takes a strict graph for the seeds and a permissive graph for the completions.
An atom on the permissive graph is kept only when its component contains a seed.
`--complete` then fills a six-ring that is missing one labeled vertex.
That walk is the least fixed point of the all-but-one rule, on
[Ring-adjacent completion](ring-completion.md).

## Confined ice {#confined-ice}

A prism block is two rings of the same size.
`ring::basalPrismConditions` is the strict test, and a pair that passes is perfect.
With shape matching on, a pair that fails that test is imperfect when `ring::relaxedPrismConditions` finds at least one bond between the rings and the shape match succeeds.
`ring::findPrisms` returns the rings that are blocks and the perfect and imperfect counts.

A monolayer analysis keeps primitive rings of each size and writes the coverage of the sheet.
The in-plane $g(r)$ normalises the pair histogram by the slab factor

$$
f(r) = 1 - \frac{r}{2h} \quad (r \le h), \qquad f(r) = \frac{h}{2r} \quad (r > h)
$$

where $h$ is the confined height.
That is `rdf2::normalizeRDF`.

## Order parameters {#order-parameters}

$$
q_l(i) = \sqrt{\frac{4\pi}{2l+1} \sum_{m=-l}^{l} |q_{lm}(i)|^2}
$$

$\bar q_l(i)$ replaces $q_{lm}(i)$ with the average of $q_{lm}$ over $i$ and its neighbours before the same sum.
That is the Lechner-Dellago form.
The implementation is `chill::steinhardtQl`.
It computes degrees 3, 4, 6, 8 and 12.
Other degrees return zeros.

<!-- https://docs.dseams.info/explanation/trace-assembly.md -->

# TRACE and signature cages {#trace-and-signature-cages}

TRACE (Hsu and Lin, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025,
[10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01459))
finds hydrate cages on a hydrogen-bond graph. d-SEAMS answers the oxygen
question: which primitive rings tile a closed polyhedron of a given face
census. The timed comparison is the how-to
[Cages and TRACE](../user/howto/cages-trace.md).

## The hydrogen-bond cage {#the-hydrogen-bond-cage}

A hydrogen bond is kept when the donor-acceptor oxygen distance is below
a cutoff and the angle at the donor oxygen, between the donated hydrogen
and the acceptor oxygen, is within the angle cutoff of a linear bond.
Rings are enumerated by depth-first search. A cup is a base ring plus
the lateral rings that share one edge with it. The cup closes when the
last lateral ring meets both of its neighbours. Complete and incomplete
cages are classified from those cups.

The TRACE program’s default cutoffs are 0.36 nm and 35°. The comparison
calls ClavisCage 0.3.18 at 0.35 nm and 35°. On an oxygen-only frame that
comparison places one hydrogen 0.96 Å from each oxygen along each of two
ice-rule bonds, then hands the waters to TRACE. d-SEAMS does not place
those hydrogens and does not call TRACE.

The three censuses in the comparison are $5^{12}$, $5^{12}6^{2}$ and
$5^{12}6^{4}$. On ice, which has no five-rings, both searches report
no cage of those three kinds. The counts are in the how-to above.

## A closed face list {#a-closed-face-list}

`seams_frame_signature` and `seams cages --signature` count a set of
primitive rings as one cage when three conditions hold. Every edge of
every face is shared by exactly two faces of the set. At least three
faces around each vertex form one cycle. The cell is a topological
sphere:

$$
V - E + F = 2.
$$

$F$ is the number of faces, $E$ the number of distinct edges, and
$V$ the number of distinct vertices. A ring whose minimum-image bond
shifts sum to a nonzero lattice vector winds through the periodic cell
and is dropped before this test. A cell thinner than twice the neighbour
cutoff is refused, because one pair can then meet through more than one
periodic image.

The default face-edge window is $[2.65, 3.15]$ in the coordinate units
of the file. `none` leaves the bound to the face census alone. On the
46-molecule sI cell, `--signature 512` reports 2 cages and 40 atoms with
the default window and with `none`.

The string `512` is twelve pentagons. `51262` is twelve pentagons and
two hexagons. `51264` is twelve pentagons and four hexagons. Joining
them with `+` prints one line per census. The call that takes the window
is `seams_frame_signature_edge`. The C API names are
`seams_signature_cages` and `seams_signature_cages_edge`.

[C++](../stable/cpp.md) documents `seams_frame_signature` and
`seams_frame_signature_edge`.
[C](../stable/c.md) documents `seams_signature_cages` and
`seams_signature_cages_edge`.

# Signature-search thread controls {#signature-search-thread-controls}

The signature search reads one OpenMP width, and the neighbour list may
narrow it. The tables record that width on hydrate cells and on ice Ic.
`threads` is the width that was requested. On the signature and kernel
tables, `cores` is the number of CPUs the process was allowed. `n` is
the number of timed calls that were kept.

## How the rows were timed {#how-the-rows-were-timed}

The signature and kernel rows at width $n$ were run with this environment:

| variable | value |
| --- | --- |
| OMP_NUM_THREADS | n |
| OMP_DYNAMIC | FALSE |
| OMP_PROC_BIND | close |
| OMP_PLACES | cores |
| RAYON_NUM_THREADS | n |
| OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS | 1 |

The process was pinned to cpu 0 when $n = 1$, and to cpus 0 through
$n - 1$ otherwise. One warm-up was dropped. Eight timed calls remain.
The median of an even count is the mean of the two central samples. The
interquartile range is the type-7 upper quartile minus the lower one.

## The width the search reads {#the-width-the-search-reads}

`seams_set_num_threads` sets the OpenMP width later calls read, and the
linkcell width with it. Zero restores the width saved at first use.
`seams_get_num_threads` reports the width the next call will request.

`seams::teamFor` returns that OpenMP width. The atom count is not read.
`seams::TeamWidth` applies the width for the rest of the call and
restores the previous width afterwards. Bond order, published CHILL+,
the k-nearest list, the shell label and local $q_l$ use `TeamWidth`.
Those calls do not start a Rayon pool.

`seams::adoptThreads` calls `prepareCompute`, then `lc_set_threads` with
the OpenMP width. `prepareCompute` calls `omp_set_dynamic(0)` and leaves
`OMP_WAIT_POLICY` as the process started it. The environment above does
not set that variable. The linkcell workers sleep between searches.
Forcing a passive OpenMP wait on top of that sleep made the next region
late by tens of milliseconds, so the OpenMP team is left running.

`lc_set_threads` stores the width of later linkcell searches. A count
below one is stored as one thread, and one thread is a serial walk. A
width keeps its pool, and a later search at the same width reuses it.
A different width uses its own pool.

The C calls `seams_signature_cages` and `seams_signature_cages_edge`
enter through `seams::FairWidth`. When `SEAMS_FAIR_WIDTH` is unset, two
forks in a row that each take more than a millisecond halve the team,
down to a quarter of the requested width. A narrowed team tries twice
its width again at most once a second. `SEAMS_FAIR_WIDTH=0` keeps the
requested width. `seams_frame_signature` and `seams cages --signature`
do not enter through `FairWidth`.

[C](../stable/c.md) documents `seams_set_num_threads` and `seams_get_num_threads`.

## The neighbour list {#the-neighbour-list}

The timed hydrate sample is one cutoff list from `neighListLinkcell`,
one depth-6 primitive-ring network, and one search of $5^{12}$,
$5^{12}6^{2}$ and $5^{12}6^{4}$ together. Below 4096 molecules that
list caps the team at four and sets the OpenMP width to the cap. The
cap is left in place, so the ring search that follows runs at four
threads as well. A request for eight threads on sI $2\times2\times2$
(368 molecules), sI $4\times4\times4$ (2944) and sII $2\times2\times2$
(1088) therefore has the same width as the four-thread row, and the
medians sit together. At 4096 molecules and above the requested width
is kept.

Several threads in that list build an orthorhombic or triclinic cutoff
with the cell-list CSR. One thread uses linkcell’s buffered walk. If the
cell list cannot be built, the call uses that walk as well. Both builders
write the same sorted cutoff set, so the ring search does not depend on
which builder ran.

`seams cages --signature` on a cutoff graph calls `neighListO`, which
does not apply the 4096 cap. The C API builds an orthorhombic cutoff
with the cell list when every atom has the requested type, and uses
`neighListO` for a triclinic frame or a frame that mixes types.

`seams_frame_signature` on a single census uses the largest face as the
depth, so `512` alone is a depth-5 network. The timed sample above
searches all three censuses on one depth-6 network.

When the pairs come from a linkcell pair list, the rows stay on the
calling thread until the frame has at least 4096 atoms and the pair
list has at least $2^{20}$ pairs. Waking a team that slept through
the search costs more than writing those rows on the caller until the
list is that large. The several-thread cell-list path does not use
that placement.

## The ring update {#the-ring-update}

`sourceTeam` sizes the enumeration of changed ring sources, and the
carried update’s full pass. The calling thread does the work until
there are about 80 sources for every worker. `teamFor` is a different
rule: it is the requested width at every frame size.

On one thread the carried update copies the new rings and sorts them
directly, then merges the rings that stay with a direct walk. Several
threads sort indices, scan for rings that meet the changed set, and
merge the rings that are kept, using `teamFor`. Dropped ring buffers
are kept and reused by the next frame.

The cage index is merged from per-thread buckets in ring order.
Membership is the sorted atom ids of each face. The census at every
width is the one-thread census.

## Eight kernels {#eight-kernels}

Eight kernels are timed on ideal ice Ic at 4096, 32768, 110592 and
884736 molecules, each at 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads. They are primitive
rings, local and cutoff $q_4$ and $q_6$, CHILL+, the shell label,
and one carried hop update. The neighbour graph is built before the
timer starts. The rings kernel is `primitive::ringNetwork` on that
graph. Local $q_4$ and $q_6$ read the same graph. Cutoff $q_4$,
cutoff $q_6$ and published CHILL+ build their own cutoff list inside
the timed call. The hop kernel times the second update, after the first
update has filled the carried state. A repeat whose fingerprint differs
from the first call aborts the run. On 4096 molecules the kernels match
the one-thread result.

`seams_frame_rings` builds the cutoff list and then searches, so its
time is not this rings kernel.

| Eight kernels on ideal ice Ic, each at 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads. n is the number of timed calls. The median of an even count is the mean of the two central samples. iqr_ms is the type-7 interquartile range. |

## The full cutoff ring call {#the-full-cutoff-ring-call}

The full call is the neighbour list, the index conversion and the
depth-6 search, timed together on ice Ic at 884736 molecules.
`cell-list` is the orthorhombic list inside that call. `linkcell` is
the buffered walk. `link`, `convert` and `search` are the three parts.
`total` is the whole call. This is not the rings kernel above.

Several threads take the half stencil one z layer at a time, in one
team. A layer stores a pair only on its own atoms. The partner row is
filled after the team has stopped, because a forward step in x reaches
back one z layer. An interior cell has no periodic image. Its thirteen
forward neighbours are plain index steps and the shift is zero, so
that cell skips the periodic-shift arithmetic. A boundary cell still
applies the shift. One thread uses the same half stencil without a
team. Below 2048 atoms the orthorhombic list runs on one thread and
then restores the caller’s width. Published CHILL+ and cutoff $q_6$
read this list. The one-thread and several-thread pair lists match.

The 4096-molecule cap and the $2^{20}$-pair row placement belong to
the signature search above. `teamFor` does not replace them.

| Ice Ic at 884736 molecules. cell-list is the orthorhombic cutoff list. linkcell is the buffered walk. total is the neighbour list, the index conversion and the depth-6 search. link, convert and search are those three parts. n is the number of timed calls. The median of an even count is the mean of the two central samples. iqr_ms is the type-7 interquartile range, filled on the total rows. |
| --- |

# Python Frame {#python-frame}

`dseams.userframe.read` in pydseamslib returns a `Frame` over
`libseams_lang`. Install with `pip install pydseamslib`.
`import pydseams` loads `pydseams.frame.Frame`.
That class has no `graph` argument on `chill_plus` and no `edge`
argument on `cages_by_signature`.
The calls below use `userframe`. The frame is
`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`, 128 oxygens, and the line under each
call is the result on that cell.

## read {#read}

```python
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> frame.n_atoms
128
```

## steinhardt {#steinhardt}

```python
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> q = frame.steinhardt(6)
>>> sorted(q)
['ql', 'ql_bar']
>>> len(q["ql"])
128
>>> round(sum(q["ql"]) / len(q["ql"]), 6)
0.625855
```

## ring_census {#ring-census}

```python
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> frame.ring_census(6)
{6: 256}
```

## rdf_2d {#rdf-2d}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> radius, values = frame.rdf_2d(tempfile.mkdtemp(), cutoff=6.0, binwidth=0.5)
>>> len(radius)
12
```

`len(radius)` is `int(cutoff / binwidth)`, here `int(6.0 / 0.5)`.
`values` is `g(r)` on those bin centers.

## monolayer_rings {#monolayer-rings}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> sheet = frame.monolayer_rings(tempfile.mkdtemp(), sheet_area=1.0, max_depth=6)
>>> sheet[6]["count"]
256
```

## find_prisms {#find-prisms}

```python
>>> import tempfile
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> frame.find_prisms(output_dir=tempfile.mkdtemp(), max_depth=4)
[{'size': 3, 'perfect': 0, 'imperfect': 0}, {'size': 4, 'perfect': 0, 'imperfect': 0}]
```

`max_depth=4` asks for prism sizes 3 and 4.
This cell’s primitive rings are the 256 six-rings, so both sizes are empty and both counts stay 0.

## to_ase {#to-ase}

```python
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> atoms = frame.to_ase()
>>> len(atoms)
128
```

## to_solvis {#to-solvis}

`to_solvis` needs solvis-tools. It returns `solvis.system.System`.

```python
>>> from dseams import userframe
>>> frame = userframe.read("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", atom_type=1)
>>> type(frame.to_solvis()).__name__
'System'
```

## `dseams.Frame` {#dseams-frame}

`import dseams` is the array module in the same pydseamslib wheel.
This repository does not build it. `dseams.Frame` stores a coordinate
array and calls `include/seams.h`. `dseams.from_ase` returns positions
and a LAMMPS cell, which `set_frame` accepts. `q4q6` returns the local
`q4` and `q6` arrays. `chill_plus()` returns labels and nine counts;
index 1 is hexagonal. `neighbours` returns a CSR, and the last offset
is the pair count. On this ice Ih cell that is 128 waters, 512
neighbour entries, 256 six-rings, mean q6 0.625855, and 128 hexagonal
labels.

For 2.14.3 the topology/local-order engine entries used by the Python
binding are:

| Python call | Engine entry |
| --- | --- |
| dseams.rings_from_csr(offsets, columns, max_depth=10) | seams_rings_from_csr / seams_graph_rings |
| ring axis_winding and contractible arrays when frame geometry is supplied | seams_rings_winding / seams_frame_ring_winding |
| dseams.tetrahedral_order(..., convention="nearest-four") | seams_tetrahedral_order / seams_frame_tetrahedral |
| dseams.tetrahedral_order(..., convention="cutoff", cutoff=...) | the same entry with all selected partners in the shell |
| dseams.local_structure_index(..., cutoff=...) | seams_lsi / seams_frame_lsi |

Centre and neighbour selections are independent zero-based arrays.  The
nearest-four convention has no distance cutoff.  The cutoff convention uses
every selected partner at or inside the cutoff and the generalized
Errington–Debenedetti normalization.  Tetrahedral order is NaN with fewer
than four neighbours; LSI is NaN without a neighbour inside the cutoff and
one beyond it.  These cases are not
reported as liquid-like zeroes.

```python
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import dseams
>>> def ice():
...     xyz, edges, reading = [], [], False
...     handle = open("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj")
...     try:
...         while True:
...             line = handle.readline()
...             if line == "":
...                 break
...             if line.startswith("ITEM: BOX BOUNDS"):
...                 edges = []
...                 for _ in range(3):
...                     lo, hi = handle.readline().split()[:2]
...                     edges.append(float(hi) - float(lo))
...             elif line.startswith("ITEM: ATOMS"):
...                 reading = True
...             elif reading:
...                 parts = line.split()
...                 if len(parts) < 5:
...                     break
...                 xyz.append([float(v) for v in parts[2:5]])
...     finally:
...         handle.close()
...     return xyz, edges
>>> xyz, edges = ice()
>>> frame = dseams.Frame()
>>> frame.set_frame(np.asarray(xyz), np.asarray(edges))
>>> frame.count()
128
>>> offsets, cols = frame.neighbours(3.5)
>>> int(offsets[-1])
512
>>> sizes, sym, hist, frac = frame.rings(3.5, 6)
>>> int(hist[6])
256
>>> q4, q6 = frame.q4q6(3.5)
>>> round(float(q6.mean()), 6)
0.625855
>>> labels, counts = frame.chill_plus()
>>> int(counts[1])
128
>>> from ase import Atoms
>>> atoms = Atoms(symbols=["O"] * len(xyz), positions=xyz, cell=edges, pbc=True)
>>> pos, box = dseams.from_ase(atoms)
>>> pos.shape
(128, 3)
>>> frame.set_frame(pos, box)
>>> int(frame.chill_plus()[1][1])
128
```

# seams CLI {#seams-cli}

The engine command is `seams`. The parser is Argum. Help, errors,
ice-type counts, and `--features` are colorized through Argum’s
`environmentColorStatus`. `NO_COLOR` turns the colors off.

```text
seams --help
seams --version
seams --features
seams read FILE
seams chill FILE
seams chill-plus FILE
seams cages FILE
seams rdf FILE
seams cn FILE
seams hbonds FILE
seams pairs FILE
seams density-z FILE
seams domains FILE
```

The same commands on the bundled multi-type frame. `pairs` and `domains`
need `--site`, so the runnable lines include it:

```bash
seams read input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams chill input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams hbonds input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams pairs input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams density-z input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
seams domains input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion,3=tail' --subset polar
```

A positional `command` and a positional `file` are required. Missing
either, an unknown command, or a parse error exits 2.

Every command accepts `--format text|json`. Text is the human-readable
format documented below. JSON writes one object per line, one object
per output frame, with the fields `schema` (`dseams.cli/v1`), `command`,
`frame`, `status`, and `text`. The `text` field is the command’s text
output, with JSON escapes for characters that need them.
`--strict-input` returns 2 when a requested
frame has no atoms; without it, empty input retains the legacy text output.
An MPI build appends a sentence to the `--last` help: under `mpiexec` the
ranks share a dump’s frames, each with `--jobs` workers, and `SEAMS_MPI=0`
keeps MPI off.

## Commands {#commands}

The `command` positional help string is `read | chill | chill-plus | ovito-chill+ | cages | symmetry | rings | prisms | cluster | fingerprint | ions | f4 | steinhardt | rdf | cn | hbonds | pairs | density-z | domains`. `chill_plus` is an accepted alias of
`chill-plus`, and `ovito_chill_plus` is an accepted alias of
`ovito-chill+` (neither alias is listed in that help string).

| command | action | stdout |
| --- | --- | --- |
| read | print the loaded cloud | nop N frame F box Lx Ly Lz and, when box.size() >= 6, xy xz yz |
| chill | CHILL labels | nop N then name count for each ice type present |
| chill-plus | published CHILL+ (shell of 4, four-nearest q3, neighbour test) | same as chill. --rule selects the rule. --layers adds phi-c P stack S. --tum-layers adds tum-phi-c P tum-stack S |
| ovito-chill+ | OVITO 3.17.2 CHILL+ (shell of 4, full-shell q3, no neighbour test) | same as chill-plus |
| symmetry | space group, one shell overlay, and the ice-label tally | symmetry backend NAME, then space-group NUMBER SYMBOL, space-group off, or space-group none. A matching whole cell adds the overlay and point-group SYMBOL N. One shell overlay, then shells LABEL N ... unmatched U. IRA, SOFI, and spglib run only when that build linked them. No atoms or no box prints symmetry needs a frame and a box and exits 2 |
| rings | primitive rings on the cutoff list. --max-ring N is the largest size (default 6). A value below 3 is read as 6 | nop N rings R then one SIZE COUNT line for each size that occurs |
| prisms | perfect and imperfect prisms of size 3 to 6 on the mutual four-nearest graph | nop N, then size S perfect P imperfect I for each size, then perfect P imperfect I |
| cluster | largest connected component of the loaded atoms | nop N largest L subset S percolation P |
| cages | ice score on six-membered rings. The four counts are disjoint and sum to the water atoms: hexagonal only, cubic only, both, water | nop N graph KIND hexagonal IH cubic IC both B water W |
| cages --signature SPEC | closed polyhedra whose ring-size census matches SPEC; each vertex lies on at least three faces that close around it, V - E + F = 2, and rings that wind the periodic cell are left out | one line per signature, nop N graph KIND signature S cages C atoms A. --incomplete adds incomplete K. --guest-types adds guests G occupied O multiple M free F, inside 1 with --inside, and occ K:N when the histogram is not empty. --shape adds shape N:GROUP |
| fingerprint | topology keys of the bonded graph | nop N graph KIND hops H method M key K classes C rings 3:a 4:b ... top key=count ... |
| fingerprint --by-atom | the summary, then one row per atom | atom I species S coord C homopolar H rings SIZE:COUNT ... |
| fingerprint --emit-library LABEL | the frame’s distinct keys as library lines | # method M hops H colors C then key LABEL rows |
| fingerprint --library FILE[,FILE...] | atoms named by key libraries | nop N graph KIND hops H method M matched X label=count ... unmatched=U and, with several libraries, depth H1=n1 H2=n2 |
| ions | ions classed by their first water shell against the seeded cages. An empty cloud prints nop 0 | nop N ice A ions I in-ice X front Y liquid Z shell S shell-ice F clusters C ions-in-ice J capped K broken B |
| f4 | Rodger F4 on H-O…O-H pairs | nop N f4 MEAN n M |
| steinhardt | cutoff-shell Steinhardt parameters for the degrees named by --l (default 4,6) and their Lechner-Dellago averages. Degrees 4 and 6 use the solid-harmonic kernel. --l 3,4,6,12 is the former four-degree line | nop N then qL A qLbar B for each requested degree, in the order given |
| rdf | partial site-site g_{IJ}(r) | # r g count then # types I J rmax R bins N volume V then one r g count row per bin |
| cn | site-site coordination number | # site-site then # types I J cutoff R cn X nI N nJ M volume V |
| cn --ions --site | cage degree on ionCloud | cage ionCloud types 1 2 cutoff R degree D nCation N nAnion M |
| hbonds | geometric hydrogen-bond count | nop N hbonds E |
| pairs --site | mutual-nearest contact pairs | contact-pair count N nCation C nAnion A |
| density-z | type-resolved \rho along one axis | # z rho then one z rho row per bin |
| domains --site | polar/apolar Stoddard component. --subset defaults to polar; tail is apolar | subset polar n N largest L P P_inf |

`chill` / `chill-plus` default to `--graph cutoff`: `nneigh::neighListO`,
every pair closer than `--cutoff`. `--graph mutual` (alias `knn`) calls
`nneigh::kNearestNeighbourList` with `k = 4`, mutual; there `--cutoff`
is only the cell-size hint (`cutoff + 1.5`). Other graphs exit 2.
Published cutoff `chill-plus` classifies in `chill::chillPlusPublishedCutoff`
(one cutoff CSR and the fused $q_3$). Every other published call goes
through `chill::applyChillPlus`, which builds that same CSR from the
neighbour rows and calls `chill::chillPlusFromCsr`. `ovito-chill+` stays
on `chill::getCorrelPlus` / `chill::getIceTypePlusNoPrint` with open
edges. `chill` calls `chill::getCorrel` / `chill::getIceTypeNoPrint`.
`--water-types T,U` is the neighbour mask (OW only); `--type` is the
load filter and is not that mask. Ice names are the
`molSys::atom_state_type` enumerators: `cubic`, `hexagonal`,
`water`, `interfacial`, `clathrate`, `interClathrate`, `reCubic`,
`reHex`, `unclassified`.

`cages` reports cage membership, not CHILL labels. Hexagonal is
HC only (Ih), cubic is DDC only (Ic), both is an atom on both,
and water is neither. The bond graph is `--graph`.

`rdf` and `cn` call `rdf::partialRdf` on LAMMPS type IDs from
`--pair-types I,J` (default `I = J = --type`). `--cutoff` is rmax. `--bins`
is optional. The volume is `nneigh::dumpVolume` (det of dump `H`).
`cn` integrates the site-site RDF to that cutoff
(`rdf::coordinationNumber`). Help text and the `cn` header say
`site-site`. `cn --ions --site` is the cage degree, documented in the
next paragraph.

`cn --ions --site SPEC` builds `site::ionCloud` and prints the mean
unlike degree of type-1 (cation) vertices from
`nneigh::neighList(cutoff, ions, 1, 2)`. The line contains `cage`.
`pairs --site SPEC` prints the size of
`nneigh::mutualNearestUnlike(ions, 1, 2)`. That line contains
`contact-pair`, not ionicity. Both need `--site`.

`density-z` calls `site::densityZ`. `--type 0` (default) keeps
every atom; `--type I` keeps that LAMMPS type. `--axis` is `x`,
`y`, or `z` (default `z`). `--bins` defaults to the bound span
over $0.1$. Each slab volume is $A_\perp \times dz$, with
$A_\perp$ from dump H (recovered `lx, ly, lz`, not bound
spans). This is not an ice score.

`chill`, `chill-plus`, and `cages` call `site::iceScoreAllowed`.
When `--family` is not `waterIce` they print `site::refuseIceScore`
(the message names the family) and exit 2. They do not fall through
to `atom_state_type::water`. Unflagged `seams chill` stays
`waterIce`. If `--family` is absent and the frame has more than two
LAMMPS types, one stderr line names `--family` and the command
still exits 0.

An empty cloud (`nop 0`) still prints. `chill` / `chill-plus` print
`nop 0`. `cages` prints `nop 0 graph KIND hexagonal 0 cubic 0 both 0 water 0`. A signature on an empty cloud prints
`nop 0 graph KIND signature S cages 0 atoms 0` for each signature.
`rdf` / `cn` still emit their headers. `hbonds` prints
`nop 0 hbonds 0`. `f4` prints `nop 0 f4 nan`. `density-z` prints
`# z rho` and zero-density bins. `ions` prints `nop 0`.

`hbonds` loads the heavy-atom cloud with `--type` and the hydrogen
cloud with `--htype`, then builds a cutoff neighbour list. Without
`--donors` it uses the water two-hydrogen-per-molecule set
(`hAtomMolList`). `--donors` passes every hydrogen index to
`populateHbondsFromDonors`. `--hdist` and `--hangle` are the acceptor-H
distance and the acceptor-centered O-O-H angle cutoffs (angle
between OO and OH). The defaults are 2.42 Å and 30 degrees, the
water values in `bond::populateHbonds`. They are not an
ionic-liquid criterion.

## Options {#options}

Names and help text are the Argum `Option` / `Positional`
definitions in `src/seams_cli.cpp`. Defaults are the C++
initializers (Argum does not write defaults into the help).

| flag | default | Argum help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| -h, --help |  | show this help message and exit |
| -v, --version |  | Print version information |
| --features |  | Print compile-time backends |
| -f, --frame N | 1 | First frame (1-based) |
| --last N | omitted (0) | Last frame (inclusive). Omit for a single --frame |
| -j, --jobs N | 1 | Parallel frame workers (OpenMP). 1 is serial |
| --rebuild | off | Recompute rings and cages on every frame. A one-worker frame range otherwise updates them from the previous frame; the output is the same |
| --format KIND | text | Output format: text (default) or json |
| --strict-input | off | Fail when a requested frame produces no atoms |
| -t, --type I | 0 | Atom type (0 guesses oxygen then type 1; density-z: 0 is every atom) |
| --resname NAME[,NAME...] | unset | Keep chemfiles residues with these names |
| --exclude-resname NAME[,NAME...] | unset | Exclude chemfiles residues with these names |
| --atomname NAME[,NAME...] | unset | Keep chemfiles atoms with these names |
| --exclude-atomname NAME[,NAME...] | unset | Exclude chemfiles atoms with these names |
| --type-map NAME=ID[,NAME=ID...] | unset | Override chemfiles atom names with positive type IDs |
| --water-types T,U | unset | Neighbour graph on these LAMMPS types only (OW). Substrate and ions never enter the 4-NN list. A type that is not in the frame is an error |
| --mol SPEC | unset | Water oxygens by molecule: water, or ids such as 1,5-12. Neighbours, CHILL, CHILL+, rings and cages then ignore ions. A missing id is an error |
| --rule NAME | published chill+ | chill-plus rule: chill+ (published default) or ovito-chill+. A path to a readable file is scanned for a rule or chill-plus key. Comments are skipped. The file is not executed as Lua or YAML. CHILL_PLUS_RULE fills an unset flag |
| --layers | off | chill-plus: literature I_sd reference from CHILL+ molecule bins (Phi_c and H/C string) |
| --tum-layers | off | chill-plus: TUM stacking from HC-basal and DDC-equatorial rings, not CHILL+ molecules |
| --shape | off | cages --signature: point group of each found cage, from those vertices only |
| --inside | off | cages --guest-types: assign by ray-parity inside the fan-triangulated faces, not nearest centroid |
| --per-atom FILE |  | chill\vert{}chill-plus\vert{}cages\vert{}fingerprint\vert{}ions: append a LAMMPS dump frame with one extra per-atom column (label, cage, class or state) for OVITO or VMD |
| --subset KIND | polar | domains subset: polar \vert{} apolar. tail is accepted as apolar |
| --by-atom | off | fingerprint: one row per atom with coordination, same-species bonds, and primitive rings through that atom |
| --max-ring N | 6 | Largest primitive ring kept by rings (default 6) |
| --pair-types I,J | I = J = --type | Pair types for site-site rdf/cn (default I=J=--type) |
| --types I,J |  | Deprecated exact alias of --pair-types. The handler prints --types is deprecated; use --pair-types on stderr |
| --family NAME | waterIce | Material family (default waterIce): waterIce, ionicLiquid, moltenSalt, des, electrolyte, confinedIL, confinedWater, networkFormer |
| --site SPEC |  | Type-to-kind map for ionCloud (1=cationHead,2=anion) |
| --ions |  | cn on ionCloud cage degree (needs --site) |
| -c, --cutoff ANGSTROM | 3.5 | Neighbour cutoff (rdf/cn rmax; hbonds heavy-atom nList) |
| --l LIST | 4,6 | Steinhardt degrees, comma-separated. Default 4,6, the solid-harmonic pair. 3, 8 and 12 are computed only when named |
| --cage-edge SPEC | 2.65,3.15 | cages --signature: keep a face only when every edge lies in LO,HI (coordinate units of the file; default 2.65,3.15). none uses the face census alone (SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE) |
| --bins N | rmax / 0.1 or box[axis] / 0.1 | Histogram bins (rdf: rmax/0.1; density-z: L/0.1) |
| --axis XYZ | z | Histogram axis for density-z (x\vert{}y\vert{}z, default z). 0, 1, and 2 are accepted |
| -k N | 4 | k for knn / seeded cages |
| --graph KIND | seeded | Bond graph. cages: cutoff \vert{} knn \vert{} knn-union \vert{} seeded. chill and chill-plus: cutoff \vert{} mutual. Help then appends the stored name, seeded unless the runtime table changed it |
| --complete | off | Seeded cages: fill the last vertex of six-rings whose other vertices carry a label (ring completion) |
| --signature SPEC |  | cages: ring-size census (4:6,6:8) or a named table entry (sodalite\vert{}alpha\vert{}512\vert{}51262\vert{}51264\vert{}51268\vert{}sh\vert{}hc\vert{}ddc); join several with + for one line each. Joined signatures share one ring network and one cage search |
| --incomplete | off | cages --signature: also report cups and incomplete cages on the ring graph |
| --guest-types T,U |  | cages --signature: LAMMPS types of guests (methane, THF, ions) placed in the found cages by their periodic centroids |
| --guest-radius R | 4.0 | cages --signature: a guest belongs to the nearest cage center within R (default 4.0) |
| --hops N | 2 | fingerprint: bonds from the center in each local key (default 2) |
| --color-types | off | fingerprint: color vertices by LAMMPS type, so species never match across types. --colour-types is the same option and is left out of help |
| --library FILE |  | fingerprint: key library (from --emit-library) to name atoms by; several, comma separated, at different hop counts name each atom by the deepest that knows it |
| --emit-library LABEL |  | fingerprint: print the frame's distinct keys as library lines under LABEL instead of the summary |
| --ion-types I,J |  | ions: LAMMPS types read against the cage assignment |
| --ion-cutoff ANGSTROM | --cutoff | ions: first water shell radius (default --cutoff) |
| --htype I | 1 | Hydrogen atom type for hbonds and f4 |
| --hdist ANGSTROM | 2.42 | Acceptor-H distance cutoff for hbonds |
| --hangle DEG | 30 | O-O-H angle cutoff for hbonds (acceptor-centered) |
| --donors | off | Use every hydrogen as a donor candidate |
| --config FILE | SEAMS_CONFIG or ./seams.env | Dotenv of SEAMS_* / LINKCELL_* knobs. Env wins over the file |
| --print-config |  | Print the resolved runtime knobs and exit |
| --tpp N | 0 (occupancy picker) | Threads per particle for the device k-NN (LINKCELL_TPP) |
| --block N | 0 | CUDA block size (LINKCELL_BLOCK / SEAMS_BLOCK) |
| --resident FRAC | 0.80 | Fraction of free device memory for a resident batch (SEAMS_RESIDENT) |
| --cell ANGSTROM | 3 | Link-cell hint so NPT frames share a grid (SEAMS_CELL) |

`--help`, `--version`, `--features`, and `--print-config` print and
exit 0 before any file is opened.

`--tpp`, `--block`, `--resident`, and `--cell` apply to the device
TUM ice score (`seams cages`) only. CHILL and $q_{lm}$ stay on
the host.

`--cutoff` is in Angstrom. `-k` also applies to `knn-union` (the
same `k` feeds `nneigh::kNearestNeighbourList`). `--graph` is used
by `cages` and `fingerprint`; a fingerprint wants one graph, so
`seeded` (two graphs) falls back to `cutoff` there. `--complete` is used by `cages` and `ions`: it
passes `true` as the fifth argument of `seededCageAffiliation`.

## `--type` {#type}

| value | single frame (load) | --last range (forEachLammpsFrame) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | LAMMPS: type 2, then type 1 if that cloud is empty. chemfiles: keep every atom. XYZ: every atom is type 1 | LAMMPS: every atom (sinp::readLammpsTrj). Classification uses cloud.pts[0].type |
| I > 0 | LAMMPS readLammpsTrjO / chemfiles filter I | LAMMPS readLammpsTrjO with that type. The CLI does not pass a coordinate slice. |

XYZ always stores type 1. Classification still uses `--type` after
the read (type 0 then becomes 1).

A mixed-type dump that is not the water guess needs `--type I`.
`density-z` treats `0` as every atom, not the oxygen guess.
See [Ionic-liquid dumps](../user/howto/ionic-liquid.md).

## Chemfiles name filters {#chemfiles-name-filters}

`--resname` and `--atomname` are include filters. Comma-separated
names within one flag are alternatives; residue and atom filters are
both required when both are present. `--exclude-resname` and
`--exclude-atomname` take precedence over includes. Names are exact and
case-sensitive.

`--type-map NAME=ID` assigns a positive d-SEAMS type before chemfiles
element inference. Several assignments may be comma-separated. This is
useful when force-field atom names encode chemically distinct sites.
Without a map, names of the form `X_suffix` use the element prefix `X`;
for example, `O_2`, `N_2`, `C_3`, `C_2`, `C_R`, and `H_` become their
atomic-number types instead of type 0. Map every carbon site separately
when the analysis must distinguish those force-field names.

For topology-free trajectories, d-SEAMS uses a same-stem topology when
present: `run.xtc`, `run.trr`, and `run.nc` use `run.gro`; `run.dcd`
uses `run.pdb`. The topology supplies residue and atom names for these
filters and mappings. The committed example is
`input/traj/confined_water_40.xtc`, with the matching GRO beside it.

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/confined_water_40.xtc --frame 1 --last 3 \
  --exclude-resname SOLX --exclude-atomname MW \
  --type-map O_2=21,N_2=22,C_3=23,C_2=24,C_R=25,H_=26 --type 8
```

## `--water-types` {#water-types}

`--type` is a load filter (one LAMMPS type, or the oxygen guess).
It is not the neighbour mask. `--water-types T,U` loads the mixed
dump (`loadType = -1`) and builds `nneigh::kNearestNeighbourList`
/ `kNearestNeighbourPair` on that type set. Ag, I, protein and
ions stay in the cloud for guests and `ions`, but they never
enter the four neighbours of OW. `chill`, `chill-plus`, `cages`
and `ions` honour the flag. Ice and cage counts are the water
types only.

```bash
seams chill-plus FILE --water-types 1
seams cages FILE --graph seeded --water-types 1
seams ions FILE --ion-types 3,4 --water-types 1
```

The same flags on the bundled multi-type frame:

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --water-types 1
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph seeded --water-types 1
seams ions input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --ion-types 3,4 --water-types 1
```

## `--pair-types` {#pair-types}

Used by `rdf` and `cn`. The Argum form is `I,J` (one comma). A bad
string exits 2 (`bad --pair-types (want I,J)`). Omit the flag to set both
sides to `--type`. These are LAMMPS type IDs on the original cloud
(site-site). `cn --ions` is a different path (ionCloud cage degree).

`--types` is a deprecated exact alias of `--pair-types`. It accepts
the same `I,J` text and prints one warning on stderr. `--type` and
`--types` both bind, because an exact name is taken before a longer
name that starts with the same characters. `--ty` matches both and
is ambiguous.

| --pair-types | single-frame load | --last range |
| --- | --- | --- |
| omitted | same as --type (one species) | same as --type |
| I,I (like) | keep type I | keep type I |
| I,J with I != J | every atom (readLammpsTrj / chemfiles unfiltered) | every atom (typeFilter 0) |

`cmdRdf` / `cmdCn` then call `rdf::partialRdf` on those two integers.
`typeOf` still resolves a zero to the first atom (or 1).

## `seams read` and the box {#seams-read-and-the-box}

`seams read` prints `gen::formatDumpBox`: the three bound spans,
then `xy xz yz` when `box.size() >= 6`. There is no separate tilt
flag. `seams rdf` uses the same dump H (`gen::periodicDist` and
`nneigh::dumpVolume`). `seams density-z` uses recovered `lx, ly, lz` for $A_\perp$, not bound spans. The in-plane sampler remains
`rdf2::sampleRDF_AA`; see
[Sheared cells](../user/howto/sheared-cells.md).

## `--graph` {#graph}

`chill` and `chill-plus` take `cutoff` or `mutual`.
The default is `cutoff`: every pair closer than `--cutoff`.
The stored configuration name of that default is `seeded`, and those two commands map `seeded` onto the cutoff list.
`--graph mutual` keeps the mutual four nearest neighbours, with candidates inside `--cutoff + 1.5`.

`cages` does not make that mapping.

| value | graph |
| --- | --- |
| seeded | mutual k-nearest seeds, union completions (ring::seededCageAffiliation; --complete sets the fifth argument) |
| cutoff | pairs inside --cutoff (nneigh::neighListO) |
| knn | mutual k-nearest (nneigh::BondGraph::KnnMutual) |
| knn-union | union k-nearest (nneigh::BondGraph::KnnUnion) |

`nneigh::bondGraphFromName` also accepts `knn-mutual` and `mutual`
as `knn`, and `union` as `knn-union`. `seeded` is handled in the CLI
and is not a `BondGraph` enumerator. Any other name throws
`std::invalid_argument` (`unknown bond graph 'NAME' (use cutoff, knn, knn-union)`) and `cages` exits 2.

Candidate cutoff for the knn graphs is `--cutoff + 1.5`.

## `--cage-edge` {#cage-edge}

Used by `cages --signature`.
Each face is kept when every minimum-image edge lies in the window.
The default is `2.65,3.15`.
`none` (also `off` or `false`) leaves that test out, and the cage bound is the face census alone, which is the search from before the window existed.
`hc` and `ddc` keep their geometric finders. The window applies to the ring-census search.

The numbers are in the coordinate units of the file.
The LAMMPS dumps in the supplied examples are angstroms, and the default covers the oxygen-oxygen contacts of the reference cells (about 2.74 to 2.81).
Set the window to the heavy-atom contact range of the model.
Widen it for a compressed cell or a guest that stretches a cage.
A file in nanometers uses `0.265,0.315`, or `none` when the contact range is unknown.
Use a comma, a colon, or a slash. `2.65-3.15` is rejected.

```bash
seams cages FILE --graph cutoff --signature 512
seams cages FILE --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge none
seams cages FILE --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge 2.4,3.4
```

The same flags on the bundled multi-type frame:

```bash
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff --signature 512
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge none
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff --signature 512 --cage-edge 2.4,3.4
```

The same string is `SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE`.
`dseams.userframe.Frame.cages_by_signature("512", edge="none")` passes it through.
`pydseams.Frame.cages_by_signature` does not take `edge`.
Lua `dseams.cages_by_signature` calls `findBySignature` and does not read a window.
The C entry is `seams_frame_signature_edge`; a null edge string is the default window.

## Runtime knobs {#runtime-knobs}

Defaults live in the binary. An optional dotenv (`SEAMS_CONFIG` or
`./seams.env`) fills unset keys. The process environment wins the
file; CLI flags win the environment. `seams --print-config` dumps
the table.

| variable | default |
| --- | --- |
| SEAMS_FRAME / SEAMS_LAST | 1 / 0 |
| SEAMS_JOBS | 1 |
| SEAMS_CARRY | 1 (0 is --rebuild) |
| SEAMS_TYPE | 0 |
| SEAMS_CUTOFF | 3.5 |
| SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE | 2.65,3.15 (none turns the window off) |
| SEAMS_K | 4 |
| SEAMS_GRAPH | seeded |
| SEAMS_FAMILY | waterIce |
| SEAMS_RESIDENT | 0.80 |
| SEAMS_CELL | 3.0 |
| SEAMS_TPP / LINKCELL_TPP | occupancy picker (0) |
| SEAMS_BLOCK / LINKCELL_BLOCK | occupancy picker (0) |
| SEAMS_OFFLOAD | false (Steinhardt Ylm and TUM cages; 0 forces host) |
| YODA_FENNEL_PATH / YODA_LUA_PATH | empty |

Analysis choice (which command) is not this table.

## File suffix {#file-suffix}

`seams` picks a reader from the path suffix
(`path.find_last_of('.')`):

| suffix | reader | included when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| xyz | sinp::readXYZ | always |
| con | sinp::readCon | SEAMS_HAS_READCON. Otherwise the command fails: readcon-core is not in this build |
| pdb, gro, dcd, xtc, trr, nc, lammpsdata | sinp::readChemfiles | SEAMS_HAS_CHEMFILES. Otherwise the command fails: chemfiles is not in this build |
| the 33 VMD molfile suffixes below | sinp::readChemfiles (chemfiles’ VMD molfile readers) | SEAMS_HAS_CHEMFILES. Otherwise the command fails: chemfiles is not in this build |
| anything else | LAMMPS dump (readLammpsTrjO / readLammpsTrj) | always |

A missing reader does not parse those suffixes as LAMMPS dumps.
`seams --features` reports chemfiles, readcon-core, and readcon-db.

that reads each and the holder of that plugin’s copyright and licence:

| xml | VASP_xml | vaspxmlplugin | University of Illinois, NCSA (molfiles/LICENSE) |
| vsf | VTF structure format | vtfplugin | University of Illinois, NCSA (molfiles/LICENSE) |
| vtf | VTF trajectory format | vtfplugin | University of Illinois, NCSA (molfiles/LICENSE) |
| xbgf | Internal Paratool Format | xbgfplugin | University of Illinois, NCSA |
| xsf | (Animated) XCrySDen Structure File | xsfplugin | University of Illinois, NCSA (molfiles/LICENSE) |

PSF, AMBER Parm, AMBER7 Parm, InsightII MDF and VTF structure format
files hold a topology and no coordinates, so every atom of such a frame
is at the origin. ABINIT, DL_POLY_4 HISTORY, VMD Tinker and Gaussian
Logfile have no suffix of their own (Gaussian’s `.log` is already
GAMESS) and the CLI does not reach them. `.out` is CPMD 3.x output;
nothing else in this tree uses that suffix for a trajectory.
[Data Formats](data-formats.md) lists every reader with its
authors, and `LICENSE.note` gives each licence.

## Frame ranges {#frame-ranges}

Omit `--last`, or set it equal to `--frame`, for one frame. That
path calls `load` and works for every linked suffix.

A range (`--last` > `--frame`) dispatches by suffix. LAMMPS dumps use
`sinp::forEachLammpsFrame`, with one handle per OpenMP worker and
deterministic output order. XYZ is a single-frame input and emits frame 1
at most. Chemfiles and readcon inputs are read serially until the requested
range or the first missing frame. The first requested frame of a
`.pdb`, `.gro`, `.dcd`, or `.con` range is an error when it is empty,
and so is a path that is missing, a directory, or not readable:
the CLI exits 2 and prints `cannot read PATH`. `--jobs 1` is serial;
non-LAMMPS readers do not use OpenMP workers.

A serial range carries rings and cage affiliation from one frame to the
next: `primitive::RingUpdater` and `ring::AffiliationUpdater` recompute only
the atoms whose bounded ball changed. LAMMPS ranges with `--jobs` above 1,
MPI ranks, single frames and `--rebuild` rebuild every frame. The output is
the same either way.

An MPI build (`-Dwith_mpi=enabled`) started by `mpiexec` shares a LAMMPS
dump’s frames among the ranks in serpentine rounds: of R ranks, rank r takes
slot r of even rounds and slot R-1-r of odd ones, so a cost that steps,
drifts or alternates along the run reaches every rank. Rank 0 prints every
frame in order; ranks past the frame count idle. Other readers stay on rank
0, `--per-atom` needs a single rank, ranks that differ in arguments,
directory or `SEAMS_` settings are refused, and color stays off unless the
environment forces it. Each rank runs `--jobs` frame workers, OpenMP threads
inside a frame, and linkcell’s rayon pool; on a launch of several ranks,
`OMP_NUM_THREADS` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` default to 1 when unset. For
hybrid runs set them per rank and bind each rank to its cores; with Open
MPI:

```sh
mpiexec -n 2 --map-by slot:PE=4 -x OMP_NUM_THREADS=4 -x RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  seams --jobs 4 --frame 1 --last 100 cages dump.lammpstrj
```

The same `seams` flags on the bundled multi-type frame, without `mpiexec`:

```bash
seams --jobs 4 --frame 1 --last 100 cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj
```

A run without a launcher, or with `SEAMS_MPI=0`, never initialises MPI.
The source notes that a singleton MPI start costs about a second.

| printed name | macro |

| Highway SIMD | SEAMS_HAS_HWY |

## Colors {#colors}

`colorizerForFile(environmentColorStatus(), stdout)`. Argum’s
`environmentColorStatus` (first match wins):

| condition | result |
| --- | --- |
| NO_COLOR set and non-empty | off |
| FORCE_COLOR set and non-empty | on |
| CLICOLOR_FORCE set, non-empty, not 0 / false | on |
| CLICOLOR_FORCE is 0 or false | off |
| CLICOLOR is 0 or false | off |
| CLICOLOR set and non-empty | allowed (TTY decides) |
| COLORTERM set and non-empty | allowed |

| --- | --- |

| shortOption | box; ice name hexagonal |
| warning | usage line; interfacial; enabled |
| error | parse / missing-args / unknown-command; unclassified, reCubic, reHex, and any other ice name; disabled |
| uncolored | water, both |

## Exit status {#exit-status}

| code | when |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | success, including --help / --version / --features / --print-config |
| 2 | parse error, missing command or file, unknown command, bad --format, bad --cage-edge, bad --axis, bad --mol, bad --subset, bad --pair-types, --bins < 0, unknown --family, ice score refused by --family, ions without --ion-types, pairs or domains without --site, cn --ions without --site, steinhardt --l outside 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, CHILL --graph other than cutoff or mutual, symmetry with no atoms or no box, a missing input file, MPI ranks that differ, or --per-atom on more than one rank |

## Examples {#examples}

```bash
seams read input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
seams cages input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj --type 1 --graph seeded
seams cages dump.lammpstrj --graph cutoff
seams cages dump.lammpstrj --graph knn
seams cages dump.lammpstrj --graph knn-union
seams chill-plus dump.lammpstrj --frame 1 --last 50 --jobs 8
seams rdf dump.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 10 --bins 100
seams cn dump.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 4.5
seams cn dump.lammpstrj --ions --site '1=cationHead,2=anion' --cutoff 6.0
seams pairs dump.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams hbonds dump.lammpstrj --type 2 --htype 1
seams hbonds dump.lammpstrj --donors
seams chill dump.lammpstrj --family ionicLiquid
```

The `dump.lammpstrj` lines on the bundled multi-type frame:

```bash
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph cutoff
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph knn
seams cages input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --graph knn-union
seams chill-plus input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --frame 1 --last 50 --jobs 8
seams rdf input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 10 --bins 100
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --pair-types 1,2 --cutoff 4.5
seams cn input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --ions --site '1=cationHead,2=anion' --cutoff 6.0
seams pairs input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --site '1=cationHead,2=anion'
seams hbonds input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --type 2 --htype 1
seams hbonds input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --donors
seams chill input/traj/il_tiny.lammpstrj --family ionicLiquid   # exits 2
```

Lua and Python are not this binary. See
[yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct)
(`require("dseams")`) and
[PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib)
(`pydseams`).
