# 2.14.3 release notes {#release-notes}

These notes describe the user-visible changes since d-SEAMS 2.13.0.
The upgrade from 2.13 is
[the upgrade guide](../user/howto/upgrade-2.14.md).

## 2.14.3 {#id1}

### Added {#added}

- The `with_openmp` Meson option, a feature that defaults to `auto`, builds every loop single-threaded without OpenMP when disabled, and stops the configure step when enabled and an OpenMP parallel region does not link.
- Fractional density profiles follow a triclinic cell axis or an arbitrary direction, with slab volumes taken from the cell. Pore profiles add a cell-edge axis and centre, cylindrical radial and azimuthal shells, and axial slabs, as number and mass density. A radial shell is the Voronoi cell of the perpendicular lattice clipped by the outer radius, times the pore-edge length. A crossing of that circle with a polygon edge is kept on the edge, including a crossing that lands on a vertex. Azimuthal sectors split a wedge, including a wedge of half a turn. Azimuth zero points along the perpendicular projection of the next cell edge, (axis + 1) mod 3. The radial coordinate is the distance to the nearest periodic image of the axis. Axis -1 selects the longest cell edge, and any other negative axis is rejected. r_max of zero covers the perpendicular face, and a negative r_max is rejected.

  Host-guest queries report the nearest framework site and contact counts by framework type. The distance is the triclinic minimum image. The shared helper is triclinicMinImage, also used by site distances, water selection, and the periodic distance functions, with the same refinement applied to batched, cached-frame, and 2D RDF (`rdf2::sampleRDF_AA` / `seams_frame_rdf2d`) distances outside the Smith ball. Outside the Smith ball it refines both the fractional wrap and, when linked, minimage’s candidate. The cell is reduced by Lagrange and Selling steps, and each reduced vector is re-evaluated from its integer coordinates in the cell with an error-free dot product. A descent then runs over the shortest member of each coset of L / 2L, which contains every Voronoi-relevant vector, so the result is the minimum image on every LAMMPS-legal cell. That includes FCC primitive, tiny tilts, tilts at `xy = lx/2` and at the corner `|xy| = |xz| = lx/2`, `|yz| = ly/2`, and elongated cells. The descent starts from the fractional wrap when probes at 3/8 of each cell edge settle within three steps and at most one of the four probes at 3/8 of the cell diagonals does not, and from the Babai point otherwise. A binary64 result is kept only when little cancelled: the Babai step subtracted lattice vectors no longer than twice the wrap, a descent from the Babai point took at most two steps, a descent from the wrap took at most three steps, and the image is at least 1/16 of the wrap. Every other image is evaluated without cancellation error, from the recorded wrap steps with exact rounding errors or from its integer lattice coefficients with error-free products and compensated sums, and kept when it clears the Voronoi cell by more than its rounding. Near ties continue in extended precision until the norm stops falling, skipping a step that does not lower the norm for the next candidate. Non-finite inputs or intermediates, singular bases, and lattice coefficients at or above 2^52 report an error without poisoning the per-thread basis cache. On the cells in `tests/test_pore.cpp`, the returned length differs from the exact minimum by at most 4 ulps of the wrapped length, 4 * 2^-52 * `|wrap|`, and by at most `1e-14` relative. Those cells are 1200 with an edge aspect ratio up to 40, 3000 each at edge aspect `1e3`, `1e5`, and `1e8`, and an aspect-`1e8` cell whose wrap is about 4e7 times its image. A positive three-length box wraps each orthorhombic axis. A box with fewer than six values does not read tilt factors. A guest type equal to the framework type is an error. framework_type 0 keeps every other type.

  Mass density is the caller’s mass unit per cubic Angstrom. A mass in amu is amu per cubic Angstrom, and multiplying by 1.66054 converts that density to grams per cubic centimetre. The library does not apply the factor.

### Changed {#changed}

- The linkcell subproject pin moves from the v0.6.0 tag to d-SEAMS/linkcell main. That commit has the CSR single-pass path, the macOS OpenMP search and runtime-path fixes, the Meson sanitize option, which links every consumer with the ThreadSanitizer runtime, and the cargo_profile option, which builds the release Cargo profile in a subproject on every Meson version. The wrap and the offline pre-seeds do not apply an exception-typeinfo patch, because the pinned linkcell carries that fix. The conda OpenMP patch and the macOS runtime-path patch are removed.
- The linkcell subproject pin moves from `0bc73576ceb4ea79909a3ad7a7931275b59a9fe4` to `d-SEAMS/linkcell` main at `f5ea5d6f0cc490686daec5e8352fdee8bc9b2314`. That commit defines `linkcell::Error`’s key function out of line in `src/error.cpp` and builds it as the shared library `linkcell_eh` (Meson `eh_shared` defaults to true; CMake `LINKCELL_EH_STATIC` is the fully static link). The wrap drops `linkcell-exception-typeinfo.patch`, and the Nix, Yggdrasil and conda pre-seeds drop the same manual patch, because the pin already contains the fix. Every target that includes the C++ headers links `linkcell_eh`, and libyodaLib keeps the one copy of the Rust archive. `gen::mic::RangeError` and `pore::BoxError` are dllexport from libyodaLib when `SEAMS_EH_EXPORT` is set and dllimport in every other translation unit, which is how the Windows build exports them; on ELF they stay one default-visibility typeinfo. The wrap and the Nix pre-seed still apply `linkcell-omp-test.patch`, which sets `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2` for linkcell’s cargo tests, because Nix’s check hook would otherwise leave that two-worker check on one thread. Remove that patch when the pin sets the variable itself; `f5ea5d6f0cc490686daec5e8352fdee8bc9b2314` does not.
- The test suite keeps each listed input and its expected value on a shorter sample. Cage fuzz keeps the first 16 trials of seed `20261101 + frames*9973 + trial*10007`, the eight half-box shifts, and the dense-graph rule. The ring oracle keeps the first 80 random graphs of seed `20261121 + threads` at one and four threads, plus the hand-built cycles, components, and ice lattices. Carried liquid frames are two consecutive frames, and the 7-frame crystal graphs, chill-plus, and the 6-frame drift stay. SIMD sizes, Ql reference values, XYZ error sentences, and tracked-file git outcomes are each one table. `docs_frame_tutorials` is removed because `docs_tutorial_interface`, `docs_tutorial_nucleation`, and `docs_tutorial_brine` already run those mains. The science brine snippet is covered by `docs_science_tutorials`, which still requires hexagonal counts 733 and 741. Those frames are vendored and returned by an in-process `urlretrieve`, and a checksum miss fails the run. Molecule stills are copied from vendored bytes, and the pixel compare stays.

### Fixed {#fixed}

- The `capi_sanitize=thread` build sets Linkcell’s `sanitize=thread` option, which rebuilds Linkcell, its Rayon pool and the Rust standard library with `-Zsanitizer=thread` (from the `rust-src` package in the pixi environment) and links the shared liblinkcell, so ThreadSanitizer sees the pool’s handoffs and joins. `capi_suite` no longer reports every chunk the pool runs as a data race when other processes keep half the cpus busy and `seams::team::run` hands its stages to Linkcell.
- `gen::mic::RangeError` and `pore::BoxError` each have one default-visibility key function in libyodaLib, and `linkcell::Error` has its key function in linkcell’s shared liblinkcell_eh. The C API, built with hidden visibility, therefore reports a minimum-image or linked-cell range failure as `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE` and a pore box failure as `SEAMS_ERR_BOX` on libc++, which matches `typeinfo` by address. `exception_typeinfo` builds a hidden-visibility shared library and fails if its `typeinfo` addresses differ.
- The exact minimum image checks that its starting image is a lattice translate of the pair’s displacement, and starts from the displacement’s own fractional wrap when it is not. With minimage 0.1.4 linked, its Euclidean image on a needle cell, such as edges 1e12, 1 and 0.4 with tilts of 0.3, is often off the lattice, and the tilted cutoff neighbour graph on that cell returned `SEAMS_OK` with pairs missing and extra. It now matches the build without minimage.
- A linked-cell search that cannot represent the frame’s cell, because an edge needs more bins than linkcell allows or the cell is too large for its cell construction, is `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE` from the C API with linkcell’s message, instead of `SEAMS_ERR_INTERNAL`. The mutual neighbour graph and the other k-nearest paths on a needle cell, such as edges 2^30, 1 and 0.375, report it that way. A non-finite coordinate reported by linkcell is `SEAMS_ERR_ARG`.
- libyodaLib no longer defines weak fallbacks for `lc_set_threads`, `lc_num_threads`, `lc_set_places` and `lc_owned_mask`. Linkcell 0.6.0, the oldest supported release, exports all four, and against a shared liblinkcell the dynamic linker bound libyodaLib’s calls to its own fallbacks, so the thread width never reached Linkcell.
- The macOS CI SDK archive is downloaded under `RUNNER_TEMP` instead of the source tree, so the checkout does not gain an untracked `MacOSX11.0.sdk.tar.xz` before the source-tree tests.
- With minimage linked, trajectory unwrapping, molecule centres, water orientation and dipole vectors, and `seams_msd_push` take a displacement past the Smith ball from the library’s bounded lattice search, as in the build without minimage, instead of minimage’s Euclidean image, which minimage 0.1.4 returns off the lattice on needle cells.
- With minimage linked, the threaded cell-list neighbour rows, the nearest unlike atom behind `seams_contact_pairs`, the batched periodic distances and the pair loop of the RDF no longer take minimage’s batched wrap as the distance. minimage 0.1.4 returns wrong wrapped distances on needle cells, some of them inside the Smith ball where the result was kept as exact. The distances now come from the library’s own fractional wrap, and minimage’s Euclidean image only starts the exact search past the Smith ball.
- With minimage linked, minimage’s Euclidean image is re-evaluated from its own lattice coefficients before the exact minimum-image search, the way the fractional wrap is. minimage 0.1.4 drops a tilt near 1e-14 of an edge, and loses tens of roundings on needle and elongated cells, and the lattice check accepted those images, so `gen::refineEuclidean`, the pore distances, the cached-frame distances and the 2D RDF returned an image off the lattice by that much. They now match the binary128 reference in `tests/mic_oracle` as the build without minimage does.
- A minimum-image range error, from a tilted cell whose minimum image needs a lattice coefficient at or above 2^52, a numerically singular cell, or a non-finite intermediate, is `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE` from the C API with the minimum-image message in `seams_last_error()`, instead of `SEAMS_ERR_INTERNAL`. Host-guest queries and the other pore calls report it the same way.
- The tilted-cell cutoff neighbour graph, CHILL, CHILL+, q4/q6 and the other paths through `gen::refineEuclidean` return `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE` on a cell outside the minimum-image range instead of keeping the fractional wrap. Keeping the wrap dropped about a fifth of the directed pairs, with `SEAMS_OK`, on a needle cell with edges 1e17, 1 and 0.4 and tilts of 0.3, at every thread count. With minimage linked, its candidate outside the Smith ball is now refined by the same exact minimum image as the other distance paths, so that cell no longer returns a wrong neighbour graph in that build either.
- No OpenMP region in the library lets an exception escape any more. The primitive-ring search and its incremental updater, cage enumeration, affiliation and packing, the cage-topology, prism and fingerprint passes, the neighbour-list and cutoff-graph builders, the C API helpers, the 2D RDF, the shell matcher and the matrix product kernels now hand an exception, such as a failed allocation, to their caller after the region instead of terminating the process. The handler that keeps the first exception no longer takes a lock, and Eigen is built with `EIGEN_DONT_PARALLELIZE`, so it opens no OpenMP region of its own.
- An exception inside a threaded neighbour, contact, CHILL, CHILL+, Steinhardt, bond-order, cage-matching, crystal-template or SOAP loop that measures minimum-image distances is returned to the caller once the loop ends, at one thread, at many threads and without OpenMP, instead of terminating the process. `seams_contact_pairs` on a cell outside the minimum-image range returns `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE` instead of aborting.
- `seams_rings_labels` and `seams_rings_labels_n` return `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE` when the prism pass meets a minimum-image range error, instead of returning the size and cage labels without the prism codes.

## 2.14.2 {#id2}

### Added {#id3}

- The stable C API (`seams_rings_from_csr`, `seams_rings_winding`) and the language ABI (`seams_graph_rings`, `seams_frame_ring_winding`) find primitive rings in a caller CSR graph. Directed edges are symmetrized, and with a periodic frame each ring reports its oriented winding along a cell axis and whether it is contractible.
- The stable C API (`seams_tetrahedral_order`, `seams_lsi`) and the language ABI (`seams_frame_tetrahedral`, `seams_frame_lsi`) compute Errington-Debenedetti tetrahedral order and the Shiratani-Sasai Local Structure Index for independent centre and partner selections. The four-nearest and cutoff-shell conventions are explicit, and a centre whose shell is too small gets NaN.
- `LICENSE.note` and `AUTHORS` give the licence and the authors of every part of the chemfiles build that d-SEAMS compiles and installs as `libseams-chemfiles`, down to the molfile plugin files under their own terms, including the DESRES DMS reader, the CPMD and Gaussian log readers, the mmtf-cpp authors and the lzma SHA-256 authors. The Data Formats page lists each molfile reader with its authors and copyright holder, and lists every plugin that is not built.
- The chemfiles that d-SEAMS builds reads every VMD molfile format chemfiles 0.10.4 can compile and that returns atoms: 33 plugins and 37 formats instead of 3. Among them are PQR, XSF, Gaussian cube, AMBER7 restart and parm7, CHARMM coordinates, Maestro, VTF, DESRES trajectories and DMS, Gromacs g96, CPMD and Gaussian logs, DL_POLY, GAMESS, and VASP POSCAR, OUTCAR, XDATCAR and vasprun.xml. `cmake/patches/chemfiles-0.10.4-molfiles.patch` enables them in the Meson and CMake builds, and the DMS reader links the system SQLite3. Counting the frames of an AMBER7 restart no longer crashes, an AMBER7 restart with no atom count on its second line no longer hangs, and an empty file or a file in which a plugin finds no atoms is an error.
- The workflow rules `h2h_release_build`, `h2h_neighbours`, `h2h_rings`, `h2h_lanes`, `h2h_asv`, `h2h_inventory`, `h2h_summary` and `h2h_campaign` run the head-to-head campaign as one chain on one shared `--core` (`h2h_core`, default `0`) with at least 12 interleaved rounds (`h2h_rounds` and `h2h_asv_rounds`, default `12`), and write a done marker under `bbdir-h2h/<stamp>/`. Running the `h2h_campaign` target on one core with `h2h_stamp=<stamp>` executes the chain; an interrupted stage resumes its run and skips the samples already recorded, and `h2h_attempt=-2` adds a suffix to the run ids, raw logs and done markers of `h2h_lanes`, `h2h_asv` and `h2h_inventory`.
- The head-to-head campaign times d-SEAMS against freud, OVITO, vesin, mdapy, pyscal3, rings-statistics-matter, SQQ, fastatomstruct and cycless for neighbour lists (a 3.5 A cutoff and the four nearest neighbours) and ring statistics on ice, mixed-phase, mW water and sII hydrate frames from 136 to 110592 molecules. `scripts/h2h_campaign.py` takes one sample per fresh process pinned to one required `--core` with single-thread environment variables and tool knobs and no warm-up call, interleaves the arms and the cells round by round with the odd rounds reversed, runs d-SEAMS twice in every cell as its own A/A band, records wall time, CPU time, peak resident memory, `os_threads`, and `calls_per_sample`, and checks round-0 neighbour-list outputs against d-SEAMS and (for `cutoff` and `knn` on frames up to 4096 molecules) against a brute-force minimum-image oracle; ring statistics (`rings`, because the oracle covers only quadratic minimum-image neighbour sets) and frames above 4096 molecules (`ice32768` and `ice110592`, due to quadratic runtime and memory cost) are excluded from the brute-force oracle and cross-checked against d-SEAMS. Its `lanes` subcommand runs the asv timing lanes with `SEAMS_BENCH_PREWARM=0` and records per-sample call and warm-up counts on every row, and the `campaign_h2h` suite exposes only valid head-to-head cells under asv. The record `data/h2h-campaign/<stamp>.jsonl` is append-only and carries the host id, pinned core, CPU model, lscpu summary, kernel, code revision, upstream base revision and commit tree on every row, and reports the actual observed OS thread counts from the record.
- The head-to-head campaign keeps fastatomstruct 2.2.0 selectable and times the release build of fastatomstruct 2.3.0 on King’s rings and local q6.
- The head-to-head campaign times local Steinhardt q6 on ideal ice Ic at 1000, 10648 and 110592 molecules, at the same 3.5 A cutoff and the same pinned serial protocol as the ring cells.
- The `ring_oracle` and `ring_oracle_python` tests compare primitive and shortest-path ring sets, ring labels and cage counts against a brute-force enumerator. They cover random graphs, edge cases (lone atoms, repeated bonds, hubs, the max-depth boundary, rings across periodic boundaries), ice Ih, Ic, II and III cells, and hand-built prism and clathrate cages, across the C++ engine, the C API and PydSEAMSlib. `scripts/gen_ring_oracle_cells.py` regenerates the ice II and III cells from GenIce2.

### Changed {#id4}

- Configure keeps an installed chemfiles only when it has all 37 VMD molfile readers and counts the frame of an AMBER7 restart. An unpatched 0.10.x has three, so configure prints how many it has and which are missing, and builds the patched 0.10.4. The probe is built with the same prefix and compilers as the rest of the build, and a compile failure is reported separately from a crash in the AMBER7 restart, mmCIF or MOL2 read. No build links a chemfiles with fewer readers.
- `seams` reads the 33 VMD molfile suffixes (`.pqr`, `.xsf`, `.cube`, `.rst7`, `.parm7`, `.mae`, `.dms`, `.g96`, `.out`, `.POSCAR`, `.OUTCAR`, …) with chemfiles. It read them as LAMMPS dumps and found no atoms. A `.log` path is GAMESS, a `.xml` path is VASP output, and a `.out` path is a CPMD log, not a LAMMPS dump. Gaussian logs are reached by format name, because `.log` is GAMESS.
- linkcell is the only neighbour backend and is always built; it needs linkcell 0.6.0, and `subprojects/linkcell.wrap` pins the v0.6.0 tag, the first release with `lc_pairs_within_csr`. Every cutoff list (`neighListO`, `halfNeighList`, `getNewNeighbourListByIndex`, `neighListPair`, the refill variants, `reusedShellList` and the `SkinNeighborList` candidates) comes from that threaded CSR query on orthorhombic, triclinic and open boundaries, and k-nearest lists come from linkcell alone. The vesin path, the in-tree cell lists, the in-tree k-nearest graph and the brute-force loops are removed, so `-Dwith_linkcell=disabled` is a configure error and the option is deprecated. The rows are the bytes the removed builders gave. A cutoff that is not finite and positive throws `std::invalid_argument`, a coordinate that is not finite throws `linkcell::Error`, a `SkinNeighborList` without a box throws, and the CHILL+ C entry points return nonzero with the message in `seams_c_error()` instead of letting the exception out.
- Public documentation now contains reader instructions and scientific results only. Maintainer workflows, repository policy, provenance pins, and video-production notes have moved out of the published manual.
- `scripts/release_build.py` also builds `libseams`, `bench_stages`, `bench_ddc_ladder` and `bench_shell_scale`, the binaries the asv lanes run.
- `tests/test_seams_input.cpp`’s `seams_input` suite passes all 77 test cases, but its total assertion count varies between runs. One case (`tests/test_seams_input.cpp:1190`, “replacing a dump during the index does not fault”) races a background thread against 300 dump rewrites on the main thread and asserts once per loop pass the background thread completes, so how many passes finish before the main thread stops it depends on OS thread scheduling.
- The three large example trajectories now live in the public `d-SEAMS/seams-core-inputs` Hugging Face dataset. Benchmarks and documentation fetch them through `input/fetch.py` with SHA-256 verification, while the test suite uses small committed fixtures and remains offline.

### Removed {#removed}

- `src/include/external` is gone. `cxxopts.hpp`, `backward.hpp` and `rang.hpp` are now Meson WrapDB wraps (`subprojects/cxxopts.wrap`, `subprojects/backward-cpp.wrap`, `subprojects/rang.wrap`), each requested with `dependency(..., fallback: ...)`, so a system package satisfies them too. `argum.h`, the CLI’s locally patched argument parser, moved to `third_party/argum/` (see its `NOTICE.md` for the patch and why it is not wrapped); `iralib_interf.h` moved to `src/include/internal/`. A new `with_backward` auto feature controls the pretty-stack-trace build. `subprojects/packagefiles/backward-cpp` overlays WrapDB’s own `backward-cpp_1.6-6` packaging with its two upstream-crashing demo executables removed from `meson.build`, since they otherwise build as default targets and fail to compile under `-Dwerror=true`; the overlay stays applied under `--wrap-mode=nodownload` too, through the wrap’s `patch_directory` key. The conda-forge recipe, the Yggdrasil build, and the Nix package all keep `with_backward` enabled and the packaged `seams` CLI still prints a backtrace on a crash: each pre-seeds `subprojects/backward-cpp-1.6` with the upstream v1.6 tarball plus that same packagefiles overlay before their network-free build step runs, so Meson resolves that one subproject from disk instead of needing a wrap fetch `--wrap-mode=nodownload` would otherwise forbid. `tests/option_names.py` resolves each WrapDB wrap’s on-disk directory from its `directory =` key instead of assuming it matches the wrap’s own name, since it does not for these three (e.g. `backward-cpp.wrap`’s directory is `backward-cpp-1.6`); and `c_api_installed`/`seams_lang_pkgconfig` now depend on the wrap’s own installed `libbackward-cpp`, since enabling `with_backward` by default means `tests_do_not_rebuild` would otherwise catch that lib as installed-but-untracked.

### Fixed {#id5}

- `third_party/argum/LICENSE` is upstream argum v2.9’s BSD 3-Clause License, Copyright (c) 2022, Eugene Gershnik, the file `argum.h` names. The conda recipe, the Yggdrasil build and the Nix package record that licence beside the project MIT licence. `tests/vendored_licenses.py` requires the file, that attribution, and those packaging records, and it still requires `third_party/csm/LICENSE.MD`.
- The asv lanes drop warm-up calls when `SEAMS_BENCH_PREWARM=0`. `CutoffIce` and `ChillPlusIce` set one OpenMP and one Rayon thread before the library loads, so they no longer time an oversubscribed thread team on one pinned core, which cost about a hundred times the serial call on a thousand molecules. `SEAMS_BENCH_PREWARM=0` drops the setup warm-up calls of `DdcArm`, `LocalQl` and `OmpScaling` and the per-operation warm-up call of `OmpScale` (`omp-session` still runs eight timed calls of each of four operations per sample). The lanes that run a binary use the release build. An arm without a source, a binary, a frame or an installed tool skips with its reason, where it used to pass without running or fail the sample. `h2h_literature` takes the release library and the running interpreter by default, `CageHeadToHead` has one class per tool so that a missing tool skips only its own arm, and `asv.conf.json` benchmarks `main`.
- `subprojects/packagefiles/backward-cpp/backward.hpp` is the header this repository used to vendor, matching upstream backward-cpp v1.6 plus the 27 commits after it. The wrap’s `patch_directory` copies that file over the v1.6 tarball, and the conda, Yggdrasil and Nix pre-seeds copy the same overlay, so those builds compile that header.
- The brine pocket census reads ice flags only at water indices, and a frame with no ice counts all its liquid water as reservoir instead of returning an empty census.
- `seams_chill_plus_graph_lammps`, `seams_chill_plus_rule`, `seams_q4_q6` and `seams_q4_q6_lammps` return nonzero and set `seams_c_error()` when an argument is invalid or the neighbour search fails, instead of letting the exception leave the C call or returning without a message.
- Release-note verification renders each release draft in-process through the builder command instead of spawning a nested Python subprocess per release, keeping the changelog verification checks within their time limit under AddressSanitizer.
- A second fuzzing pass over the fixed readers found more crashes, now fixed with a fixture each under `input/hostile/`: GAMESS gradient and coordinate rows past the atoms counted, BGF and XBGF records shorter than their columns and CONECT records past the bonds counted, VASP XDATCAR and POSCAR atom counts that overflow an `int`, signed shifts in the js and Gromacs byte swaps, a LAMMPS dump without its `NUMBER OF ATOMS` item or with an atom id out of range, an MMTF transform matrix that is empty or short, TNG string blocks freed or filled with the wrong counts, a TNG file that declares far more particles than it stores positions for, a TRR frame with atoms but no positions, velocities or forces, an empty SMI square brace, a TPR function type outside the GROMACS table, and an extended XYZ comment with an `=` that has no name before it (the parser looped on it). TNG now refuses a frame set whose blocks leave a particle without values instead of returning uninitialised memory. The VTF reader no longer parses a line containing NUL differently on the second open of a file, which made `nsteps()` pass a null handle to the plugin; it now joins continuation lines ending in `\`, which it never did.
- A fourth hardening and fuzzing pass under AddressSanitizer, UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer and LeakSanitizer fixed all remaining memory leaks, out-of-bounds reads, integer overflows and hangs across the vendored chemfiles readers and bundled libraries, with regression fixtures under `input/hostile/`: `Molfile<F>` now closes plugin handles with RAII when `read_topology()` throws from the constructor; `gaussianplugin`, `cpmdlogplugin`, `gamessplugin`, `gromacsplugin`, `moldenplugin`, `carplugin`, `cpmdplugin`, `vaspposcarplugin`, `dmsplugin`, `vtfplugin`, `mdfplugin`, `abinitplugin`, `xbgfplugin`, `ReadPARM.h` and `Gromacs.h` release allocated handles, statements and buffers on error paths and guard null or out-of-bounds pointers; `TNG` uses RAII buffers, bounds compressed unpacking in `coder.c` and `tng_compress.c`, bounds data-block allocations against file length, rejects non-monotonic frame-set navigation offsets and frees `tng_gen_block` and `molecule_cnt_list` on error; `PDB` guards empty `atom_offsets_` in `CONECT`, nucleic `O3'`/`O5'` lookups, zero `HELIX` class and empty `decode_hybrid36` inputs; `MMTF` throws `FormatError` instead of asserting on `atomSkip_ > id`, validates `chainsPerModel`/`groupsPerChain` totals and bounds MessagePack sizes; `gemmi` prevents signed integer overflow in `atox.hpp` and `numb.hpp` exponents; and `CSSR`, `SDF`, `LAMMPSData`, `MOL2`, `AmberNetCDF`, `XYZ` and `XTC`/`XDRFile` guard short lines, empty splits, huge extended property repeat counts and integer overflows.
- Every format the chemfiles build enables was fuzzed under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, and each crash, hang and sanitizer report is fixed in its reader. A truncated AMBER7 parm or parm7 file, a Gaussian cube with a huge atom count, an mmCIF row without its model column, a one-byte Maestro file, a PQR line that starts with NUL, a BINPOS atom count that overflows, and hostile DESRES, js, XSF, XBGF, CAR, DL_POLY, g96, TRJ, XTC, TRR, TPR, DCD, Amber NetCDF, CSSR, GRO, SMI, TNG and MMTF files are errors. A VTF reader that runs out of memory keeps its bond count, and the molfile and LAMMPS Data readers define `S_ISREG` where the C library lacks it (MSVC). Each fix has a fixture under `input/hostile/` that `chemfiles_hostile` reads.
- A text file with a line longer than chemfiles’ read buffer keeps the right offset for the steps after it. The next frame of such an XYZ file was read from the wrong place, and an SMI file with such a line and a blank tail looped forever. The mmCIF writer prints `?` for an empty atom name or type, which the reader reads back as empty, so the row keeps its columns.
- VTF reads a declared atom count of any size that fits in the signed index and in the allocation, including the 201000, 330000 and 1000002 atom structures the 200000 ceiling refused. Extended XYZ keeps every property whose columns are on the atom line, including a 5000-wide SOAP vector, and reports a repeat the line does not carry. TNG XTC2 and XTC3 check every read and write against the packed length, and the Huffman decoder sorts code lengths the way upstream TNG does, so a valid BWLZH or XTC3 frame decodes and a short or unordered table fails cleanly. The run-length, LZ77, move-to-front and Burrows-Wheeler stages return an error instead of reading off their buffers, and the compressor allocates the packed block it measured. A DESRES trajectory opens from its directory or from the empty clickme.dtr inside it once the directory has the timekeys, frame files, metadata and .ddparams the DESRES reader expects; a clickme.dtr outside such a directory is refused and any other empty .dtr file is reported as empty. binpos rejects an atom count the file is too short to hold before allocating it, and a TNG particle array is sized from the decompressed block rather than from a 4096:1 ratio of the file. GAMESS refuses a log whose basis function count is negative or too large for the coefficient table it sizes, instead of allocating from it.
- A truncated InsightII MDF, an over-long AMBER7 parm token, a long or hostile VTF record, an AMBER7 restart whose atom count does not fit in the file, and a VMD Tinker file with that kind of count are errors. They used to crash or hang inside the molfile plugin. A header count larger than the file is an error for the other dense molfile readers too. A whitespace-only mmCIF, a LAMMPS Data file with no section, a LAMMPS atom count that does not fit, and an XDR record longer than the file (TPR, TRR, XTC) are errors as well.
- `sinp::openFrame` and `seams_system_read` now refuse chemfiles-only trajectory formats (`.pdb`, `.gro`, `.dcd`, `.xtc`, `.trr`, `.nc`, `.netcdf`, `.tng`, `.mmtf`) with `chemfiles is not in this build; <ext> input needs it` instead of falling through to the LAMMPS dump reader when built with `-Dwith_chemfiles=disabled`, and `trajectory_python` asserts that refusal in chemfiles-off builds.
- A GAMESS log and a valid CPMD output read through chemfiles. The molfile reader passed a null QM timestep to plugins that parse each frame in `read_qm_timestep_metadata`, which it never called, so both crashed; the Gaussian and Molden readers take the same guard. A CPMD output with an over-long version line is an error instead of a stack overflow.
- The vendored chemfiles `span.hpp` constructor omits its unused `size` parameter name under `NDEBUG` via `cmake/patches/chemfiles-0.10.4-span-unused.patch`, and `tests/ring_oracle.hpp`, `tests/test_ring_oracle.cpp` and `tests/test_chemfiles_hostile.cpp` cast signed indices to `std::size_t` or `std::ptrdiff_t`, so Clang 21 and GCC 15 builds pass with `-Dwerror=true`.
- Vendored Chemfiles installs its shared library when seams-core is built as a Meson subproject.
- Precompute exact periodic minimum-image bond vectors via `gen::relDistFromPoint` in `chill::specializedChillPlus` so triclinic cells use full tilt-aware MIC instead of orthorhombic `mic1`, and clamp `dz / r` and zero-distance bonds in `y3`.
- The chemfiles name-filter example in the CLI reference runs on `input/traj/confined_water_40.xtc`, the committed three-frame confined-water trajectory with its same-stem GROMACS `.gro` topology.
- Unwrap cluster atoms in `clump::recenterClusterCloud` along a BFS spanning tree of the neighbour list `nList` rather than Stoddard’s linked-list cycle, preventing clusters spanning more than half a box edge from being split across periodic boundaries.
- The Meson dist script does not run when seams-core is a subproject.
- Remove the trajectory dataset revision hash from documentation pages so only `input/fetch.py` stores it, and flag dataset revision hashes in source and rendered documentation checks.
- Split documentation reader-text checks from live package-registry validation. The offline check still parses install claims. Live registry claim checks run in a dedicated docs workflow job.
- Initialize `ylm` rows, divide by the count of non-zero-distance bonds, clamp `cos(theta)`, and guard zero-norm denominators in `chill::getq6`, and guard empty `c_ij` lists in `chill::reclassifyWater`.
- The head-to-head campaign provenance check caches Git object and commit lookups per run, and the AddressSanitizer Python launcher drops the sanitizer preload for Git subprocesses so the check completes within its time limit.
- Files with `.lammpsdata` and `.data` suffixes use the Chemfiles LAMMPS Data reader. Frame counting validates the coordinate frame and reports failure for a malformed file.
- Reading a malformed `.lammpsdata` file, or one with an unrecognized header keyword line, is an error. Release builds of the vendored chemfiles 0.10.4 spun forever on such a file; a patch makes the reader throw a format error, and the system-library probe rejects a copy that still spins.
- Mutual and seeded graphs in the language bindings keep a pair only when its minimum-image distance is strictly inside the cutoff plus 1.5 Å. `kNearestNeighbourList` and `kNearestNeighbourPair` take that length only as a cell-size hint, and `pairs_within` applies the distance test in `bond_list`, on the mutual chordless graph, and on the seeded cage graphs.
- On an empty frame `seams_frame_q4_q6_chill` returns zero counts. It now rejects a cutoff that is zero, negative or not finite.
- The Linux archive, conda recipe, and Julia build include the Linkcell licence for the neighbour backend compiled into libyodaLib.
- The glibc 2.28 release build gives the extracted source to the container user and replaces the packaged readcon checkout before pinning it.
- Campaign dry runs can plan on macOS. Recording timed samples still requires Linux CPU affinity.
- The bundled Linkcell build finds the OpenMP headers and runtime in the active conda environment on macOS.
- The bundled Linkcell adds the libomp runtime directory to Cargo-built Mach-O targets so they can load Conda’s OpenMP library on macOS.
- The Nix package source includes `scripts/dist_strip_vcs.py`, which Meson reads when it finds Python. The development shell omits the workflow runner that depends on the broken `stopit` package. Source snapshots preserve the tracked-file inventory used by the docs checks.
- The core Nix flake uses Nixpkgs 26.05 on Intel macOS, selects OVITO and Qt test wheels for each platform, and enables optional engines when Nixpkgs provides them for the target. The legacy Python wrapper in the Nix check uses the bundled Linkcell headers. The Nix build uses patched Chemfiles for trajectory reading and links the LAMMPS plugin against an MPI-enabled LAMMPS build.
- `pixi run test` and `pixi run coverage-run` now install `pydseamslib` (`dseams` and `pydseams`) automatically when missing before running the test suite, and the Python binding installer removes its temporary build directory on exit.
- The PLUMED 2.10 engine environment now includes pytest, so bindings configure in that lane instead of failing at configure time.
- `scripts/install_pydseamslib.sh` now runs in a source tree without `.git`, such as an unpacked `meson dist` tarball: `--if-missing` reports that an existing install cannot be matched to that tree and reinstalls, and the install stamp records a null tree that no later `--if-missing` accepts.
- `seams read` exits 2 and prints `cannot read <path>` when a PDB, GRO, DCD, or `.con` path is missing, empty, a directory, or not readable, and when a type filter keeps no atoms. A file that opens and contains atoms is unchanged.
- The README names the public dataset and `python3 input/fetch.py` without repeating the dataset revision. The fetch helper keeps that revision in `input/fetch.py` and downloads it.
- `seams_rings_labels` and `seams_rings_labels_n` now label every six-ring of ideal ice Ih as a hexagonal-cage face (N/2 basal, 3N/2 prismatic) on the cutoff graph of an orthorhombic box. The label pass rebuilt its neighbour rows from the cutoff CSR without the leading self entry that the cage and prism tests skip, so each atom lost one bond: 668 of the 8192 six-rings of a 4096-molecule ice Ih cell came back as plain `SEAMS_RING_HEXAGON`, and prism labels read the same short rows. Triclinic frames and the mutual graph were not affected.
- `primitive::countAllRingsFromIndex` with `removeNonSPrings` lists each ring once when a neighbour row repeats a partner, and no longer reads past an empty row. It now returns the same ring set as `primitive::ringNetwork`, which already dropped repeats.
- The science tutorial check has a 600 s timeout and runs serially in AddressSanitizer builds.
- Refine triclinic displacements with exact Euclidean minimum-image reduction outside the Smith ball in `passTilt` (`src/cutoff_csr.cpp`) and in Steinhardt and CHILL/CHILL+ bond-vector kernels (`src/steinhardt_parallel.cpp`, `src/bop.cpp`), and use `floor` for fallback cell counts in `orthoChill`.
- Compute triclinic fractional coordinates `(sx, sy, sz)` before wrapping to `[0, 1)` in `cutoffSolid` and `chill::q4q6ChillPlus`, so atoms shifted into periodic images outside the primary cell keep exact tilt coupling.

## 2.14.1 {#id6}

### Added {#id7}

- The linux-x86_64 tarball carries LICENSE and the license texts for Eigen, argum, backward-cpp, readcon-core, readcon-db, and the GCC runtime objects in its binaries.
- The release upload now checks the linux-x86_64 tarball in fresh Ubuntu
  22.04, Rocky Linux 9, and Debian 12 containers. Each check compiles
  `docs/examples/quickstart.c` with the `pkg-config` flags for `seams` and
  runs it on an eight-molecule ice frame.

### Changed {#id8}

- On glibc the first library call raises the heap trim threshold to 256 MiB and the mmap threshold to 32 MiB, so the buffers one call frees are reused by the next instead of being faulted in again. The same call varied by 10 to 30 percent between runs before. The setting is process-wide; `SEAMS_MALLOC_TUNE=0` skips it, and a caller that set `MALLOC_*_` or a `glibc.malloc` tunable keeps its own values.
- The k-nearest neighbour graph scales with OpenMP threads. linkcell 0.4.3 scatters the k-nearest mesh by bin owner, builds the graph rows and the CSR in the search’s own parallel region and keeps a one-thread search on one thread; no OpenMP team is started for the call. Neighbour order is unchanged, ties included, at every thread count. On 110592-molecule ice Ic in the omp-scaling sitting of source tree 1c41a929, `seams_neighbours_knn` with four neighbours takes 40.6, 22.5, 13.0 and 7.9 ms at 1, 2, 4 and 8 threads instead of 58.2, 45.6, 37.0 and 33.2; on 884736 molecules it takes 62.5 ms at 8 threads instead of 279.8. In the same sitting OVITO takes 17.7 ms, mdapy 2.0.0 17.0 ms, freud 3.6.1 23.7 ms and pyscal3 4.1.0 103.5 ms for the same graph at 8 threads.
- The linux-x86_64 release notes record the glibc version, OpenMP runtime, pkg-config prefix, and binding versions measured for that build.
- Linux release binaries build inside manylinux_2_28 and need glibc 2.28 or newer.
- The linux-x86_64 archive loads the system OpenMP runtime (`libgomp1` on Debian and Ubuntu, `libgomp` on RHEL).
- The pixi full-suite now fails whenever a test is skipped, so a passing
  run confirms that the required analyses and documentation checks all ran.

  `-Dwith_lammps=enabled` now requires the LAMMPS class headers needed for
  `compute dseams`; Meson errors unless `lammps_src_include` points to
  matching sources.
- Rings with symmetry codes build the atom-to-ring index on the team and no longer copy a frame whose rings all have one size before the cage and prism passes. `seams_rings_find` on 110592-molecule ice Ic takes 31.3 ms at 8 threads instead of 36.6, 4.1 times faster than 1 thread instead of 3.5, and 302 ms instead of 358 on 884736 molecules. The 1-thread times are no slower, and every label is identical to the previous build at 1, 3 and 8 threads.

### Fixed {#id9}

- The sanitizer suite does not preload libasan into the test harness. Interpreter wrappers and the cargo test runner map it for the process that hosts libseams. Host shells, compilers, and `mpirun` do not inherit it. `pin_host` exports the runtime only to its MPI ranks, turns off Open MPI’s memory patcher for that launch, and turns leak detection off for those ranks. Open MPI and PMIx keep allocations until the rank exits, and those frames are not added to the suppression list.
- The cage invariance fuzzer sizes its trial pool to the CPUs the process may run on.
- Ring and cage search diagnostics stay on the calling thread. Concurrent searches no longer share the process-global profile, phase and split records, and an OpenMP team copies the calling thread’s flags when it starts.
- C API fuzzers built with `b_sanitize=thread` link `-fsanitize=thread,fuzzer` and the shared thread runtime.
- A ThreadSanitizer death fails the TSan C API suite. The suite runs with `exitcode=0` so that the libgomp barrier races do not fail it, and that was also the exit status of a FATAL, a CHECK failure or a deadly signal, in the suite and in each `capi_cpp_ref` it starts, so a crashed reference still left “capi suite ok”. `abort_on_error=1` makes such a death SIGABRT, and `tests/capi_tsan_gate.py` passes the suite only on exit 0, a “capi suite ok” line, and no ThreadSanitizer output but data races among the main thread and the libgomp workers it started.
- d-SEAMS builds against an installed chemfiles 0.10.4 or a later 0.10 release, including the copy in Chemfiles_jll. The build finds it through `-Dchemfiles_dir`, pkg-config or the CMake package. A cross build with `-Dwith_chemfiles=auto` that finds no chemfiles stops with an error that lists the places it searched, and never builds a copy for the build machine. The option `-Duse_vendored_chemfiles` takes `auto`, `enabled` or `disabled`. CMake builds take `SEAMS_CHEMFILES_DIR` and `SEAMS_USE_VENDORED_CHEMFILES`. With an installed chemfiles 0.10.4, d-SEAMS refuses a MOL2 file with no counts line and an mmCIF file with no `label_entity_id` column and an unset `label_seq_id`. Each gives a message where it used to crash.
- Malformed MOL2 and mmCIF files that chemfiles refuses now report a read error through the C API and every language binding instead of returning a frame with zero atoms.
- The documentation build rewrites sitemap entries to lowercase extensionless routes after the link and metadata pass, and video end cards no longer include publication-status text.
- The docs workflow check reads `contents: write` from the build-deploy job and stops at the next job.
- The docs publish job drew every molecule still twice at 4096 px and 256 samples, so Publish the book sat on the runner for hours. The delivered pictures are 2048 px, and a denoised 64-sample frame at that size matches the old stills. The job now stops if it runs for more than two hours.
- The k-nearest degree scan starts after the linkcell pool joins, so it no longer reads a row while that row is still being stored.
- The serial LAMMPS hook calls `lammps_mpi_finalize` after `lammps_close`, which frees the ReadData and Run commands the stub would otherwise leave allocated. The MPI build still calls `MPI_Finalize`.
- The fused k-nearest graph and linkcell’s stage runner are used when that library provides `lc_knearest_csr` and `lc_team_run`. A linkcell 0.4.2 build keeps the in-tree graph and the OpenMP stages.
- `seams.pc` and the other pkg-config files in the Linux tarball use `prefix=${pcfiledir}/../..`, so the link line follows wherever the tarball is unpacked.
- The release recipe enables the .con reader when `SEAMS_WITH_READCON=enabled`. A checkout that already contains the readcon wrap leaves the reader off, as does the conda-forge archive.
- `seams_system_read` in the Linux tarball reads .con files, because the release build turns the readcon reader on.
- Source archives now include every subproject, the patched chemfiles
  source, and pinned tutorial inputs, so users can build and test in
  offline environments.
- Library calls cope better when other processes keep the cores busy. Placement reads the threads other processes have runnable: beside a few it narrows the team to the free cpus and leaves it unplaced, and beside half the mask or more it leaves the team to the scheduler and runs the cutoff list, cutoff q_l, CHILL+ and the shell match as stages whose chunks linkcell’s pool claims, so no stage waits for a worker the scheduler has parked. A lone team narrower than the mask is not pinned. Linkcell’s pool keeps the requested width when the OpenMP team is narrowed, the k-nearest graph passes are handed out in parts, a full-width fork that waits out a time slice halves the team at once, and the frame calls of the R and Julia fronts narrow as the C API does. Beside an 8-thread spinner on 8 cores, the 884736-molecule k-nearest graph takes 114 ms bound and 110 ms unbound instead of 345 and 365 (OVITO 209 and 207), and on 110592 molecules 20.0 ms bound and 19.1 ms unbound instead of 54.5 and 59.1 (OVITO 28.2 and 28.3). q6 on 110592 molecules takes 12.2 ms bound and 11.1 ms unbound (OVITO 23.6 and 23.2).
- Worker placement now stays inside the host mask and is undone when the call returns. `SEAMS_PIN=0` leaves placement to the host. `OMP_PROC_BIND`, `OMP_PLACES`, `GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY`, `KMP_AFFINITY`, and a caller already bound to one cpu are left as the host set them. Several copies of the program share the mask in disjoint slices instead of all pinning worker i to cpu i.
- An unbound 8-thread team no longer stalls when another thread is runnable. When the team fills the mask on an otherwise idle machine, workers take one allowed cpu each unless `OMP_PROC_BIND` is already set, and linkcell’s pool keeps that cpu list instead of inheriting the caller’s pin. With only `OMP_NUM_THREADS=8`, neighbours and q6 on 110592-molecule ice Ic take 2.4 ms each in one fresh process, ahead of the 13.0 ms (OVITO q6) and 17.0 ms (mdapy k-nearest graph) rival times.
- The in-situ reporter returns the five-item descriptor tuple required by OpenMM 8.0.
- The default pixi environment installs OpenMM on macOS, so the OpenMM engine page and the engine walkthrough run it there. The two scripts load `e2e_common` by file. `engines/openmm` on `sys.path` imported as an empty package and hid the missing module until `import openmm.app` failed.
- The four-process placement check runs on a four-cpu mask. Each process keeps one cpu, and a sample counts that cpu. A lone process still has to show two cpus in the same sample.
- `pin_host` is registered on Linux only. It reads cpu masks with `sched_getaffinity` and the proc filesystem, and the placement it checks exists only on Linux. On macOS it stopped at the missing `libyodaLib.so`, and it could not have passed with the dylib either.
- The 2.14 release-notes page title names 2.14.1 instead of 2.14.0.
- The science tutorials and the science snippet pages run the Julia and R tutorials from the bindings they moved to. With `julia` on PATH, the Julia leg runs `examples/science_tutorials.jl` of the developed Dseams.jl against this build’s libseams; with `Rscript`, the R leg runs the `examples/science_tutorials.R` that the installed dseams package carries. They ran `docs/examples/science_tutorials.jl`, `science_tutorials.R` and `science_r.c`, which left with the bindings, and failed wherever Julia or R was installed. A missing Dseams.jl or dseams fails the tutorial and names the binding.
- The science tutorial check keeps a 180 s timeout, and allows 900 s when `b_sanitize` is set. Alone under AddressSanitizer the tutorial takes about 24 s; in the full sanitizer suite it shares the cores and takes more than 180 s.
- The sH cell header snippet compiles with the C compiler the build was configured with, and without the suite’s library path, so the loader opens the libc that compiler linked.
- `scripts/sanitize_thread.sh` links with the host `ld`. The conda `ld` took `libdl.so.2` from the conda sysroot and libc from the host, so meson rejected `-fsanitize=thread`. `scripts/build_tsan_openmp.sh` builds Archer from the LLVM release that matches clang. A libomp from an older release left `__kmpc_dispatch_deinit` undefined when the tests loaded it.
- A ThreadSanitizer build gives plumed, gmx and lmp the unsanitized plugin, because those hosts cannot map `libclang_rt.tsan`. Interpreter shims map that runtime before they dlopen `libseams`.
- Replaying the video tapes compares the replayed output, the seams census and the rest of the run with recorded.txt, and no longer treats a LAMMPS warning or its docs URL as part of that result.
- `chill::cutoffSolid` calls `seams::ylm::ylmAdd8` only when `SEAMS_YLM_AVX512` is set. That function is built only on x86-64. The call used to stay in the binary at -O0 on every other machine, and a debug macOS arm64 link failed with the symbol undefined. `ylm_add8_o0` compiles that file at -O0 without the flag and rejects an undefined `ylmAdd8`.

## 2.14.0 {#id10}

### Added {#id11}

- The manual has a Use with AI assistants page. skills/d-seams/SKILL.md tells an agent how to install the engine and call it, and llms.txt links the Markdown twin of each page.
- The binding-overhead session times each language wrapper of read, k-nearest neighbours, q6 with q6bar, CHILL, and primitive rings on ice Ih, and records the median and interquartile range.
- A CI job compiles the library sources PydSEAMSlib and dseams-r build under Clang 22 with `-Wsign-conversion -Wunneeded-internal-declaration -Werror`, once without OpenMP or any optional backend and once with them, and builds those libraries with `-Dwerror=true`. The compiler-warnings workflow also runs on `release/**` branches.
- The installed C library reads frames from arrays and files. Callers can build neighbour lists and primitive rings, evaluate q3, q4, q6, and q6-bar, and run CHILL, CHILL+, cages, the shell classifier, and the brine front. `seams.pc` and `seams-config.cmake` ship with the library, and `examples/c` builds against that install.
- `Frame.cages_by_signature` takes `edge`, and Lua `dseams.cages_by_signature` reads `edge` from its options table. Both call the same window as `--cage-edge`: empty keeps `2.65,3.15`, and `none` leaves the cage bound to the face census. The C entry for the libseams path is `seams_signature_cages_edge`. `seams_frame_signature_vertices_edge` returns the vertices of that window.
- `capi_abi_2_13` holds `libseams_lang`, the C interface of the 2.13.0 release (`seams_lang.h`), to that release’s ABI: it compares a debug build of the library with the libabigail corpus in `scripts/abi_2.13.0_seams_lang.abi`, passes functions added since, and fails on a removed function or a changed signature. `capi_abi_2_13_selftest` edits copies of the corpus to prove both failures are caught. The `capi-abi` CI job runs both. Without `abidiff` they are skipped.
- `capi_abi` compares libseams type by type with the 2.14.0 ABI 1 corpus through libabigail’s `abidiff` when it is installed, and passes only added functions. The `abi` pixi environment provides `abidiff`, and the `capi-abi` CI job uses it. Without `abidiff`, or with one too old to read the corpus, that step is skipped.
- Julia, R, and C++ call the analyses `seams.h` now exports. Julia uses `ccall` on `libseams`. R keeps the `libseams_lang` frame API and adds a C shim. `seams.hpp` is a header-only RAII wrapper whose exceptions carry `seams_handle_error`.
- The Rust, Fortran, and Python ctypes bindings call the analyses `seams.h` now exports, including frame reading, CHILL, Steinhardt parameters, cages, neighbour lists, the RDF, hydrogen bonds, density, the fingerprint, prisms, and the monolayer.
- `capi_docs_complete` fails when a function in `tests/capi_symbols.txt` lacks a `seams.h` doc comment with a brief, every parameter, the return codes, thread safety, and ownership for pointer arguments, or when its C API page section is missing or differs from that comment. `capi_docs_selftest` removes each of those pieces from a copy of the header or page and requires the check to report it.
- `docs/examples/c/` holds one short C program per C API family: neighbours, rings, CHILL+, q4 and q6, cages, and errors. Each checks its own results on the in-tree ice Ih fixture, and `capi_example_<family>` compiles it as C11 with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror` and runs it. The C API page includes all six.
- C API: `seams_system_set_positions` overwrites the coordinates, and optionally the cell, of a stored frame, and `seams_system_box`, `seams_system_positions`, `seams_system_types`, and `seams_system_ids` copy the stored frame back out through a const handle. `seams_system_set_atoms` reuses the storage of the frame it replaces, and keeps the id index when the ids are 1 to n, so loading 110592 atoms costs about the same as building the frame in C++.
- `-Dcapi_fuzz_coverage=true` instruments this project’s code for libFuzzer under clang, so the fuzzers see coverage inside `libseams` and not only in the harness. Subprojects stay uninstrumented, so their examples link without a sanitizer runtime; with sanitizers or coverage on, clang links the shared libraries with `-z undefs` and leaves the runtime’s symbols to the executable.
- `capi_installed_examples` installs libseams into a staging directory and builds the six family examples in `docs/examples/c` out of tree against it, once with the flags from `pkg-config seams` and once through `find_package(seams)` with the new `docs/examples/c/CMakeLists.txt`, both as C11 with `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`. Every binary must load the installed `libseams.so` and pass its own checks.
- `seams_c_last_stages` returns the wall seconds of the last `seams_cutoff_csr` or `seams_ql_cutoff` call on the calling thread, split into point-cloud conversion, cutoff-list build, q_l and copy-out.
- `capi_reload_fuzzer` drives `seams_system_set_atoms`, `seams_system_set_positions` and `seams_system_stage_positions` with random atom counts, NULL pointers, wrong lengths, NaN and infinite values in both reload modes, and reads the frame back after every call. Under clang the libFuzzer harnesses are built with `-fsanitize=fuzzer` and the `capi_sanitize` sanitizer.
- `-Dcapi_sanitize=address,undefined` builds the C API suite under ASan and UBSan at once, and every UBSan build also checks float-to-int overflow, which GCC leaves out of `-fsanitize=undefined`.
- C API: `seams_last_error_message`, `seams_system_natoms`, `seams_neighbours_nrows`, `seams_rings_nrings`, and the length-checked `seams_chill_plus_n`, `seams_q4q6_n`, `seams_rings_labels_n`, and `seams_rings_histogram_n`. Every public declaration in `seams.h` now has a Doxygen block with parameters, ownership, thread safety, and an example.
- `bench/capi_thread_scale.txt` records `capi_thread_scale` on a release build. At 8 threads the cutoff-list build is about 60% of `seams_ql_cutoff` and 74% of `seams_cutoff_csr`, and the serial point-cloud conversion about 15% and 18%.
- `capi_thread_scale` runs `seams_cutoff_csr` and `seams_ql_cutoff` at 1, 2, 4 and 8 OpenMP threads on 110592-molecule ice Ic, requires every width to return the one-thread bytes, and logs the per-stage times.
- Saved trajectories other than CON are read with chemfiles, including xyz, a LAMMPS dump, gro, pdb, dcd, xtc and Amber NetCDF. A selection expression names water oxygen and hydrogen. The dependency is optional and on by default.

The detail column records agreement on that frame. The rings row is the cutoff list and ring search together; the ringNetwork-only row isolates the ring kernel.
- A test run now fails `source_tree_untracked_check` when the run leaves an untracked, non-ignored file in the source tree that was not there when `source_tree_untracked_snapshot` ran before the other tests. Each test run keeps its own snapshot, so concurrent runs on one build directory cannot mask each other’s artifacts, and a check without a snapshot from the same run fails. `source_tree_untracked_parallel` reproduces two such runs. The run is found from `/proc`, or from `ps` where `/proc` is missing or cannot read a process; when neither can, both tests fail with a message.
