### seams_water_vectors {#id125}

Purpose: Water orientation vectors: O to H-midpoint and H-to-H under PBC.

Each water pairs one oxygen_type atom with two hydrogen_type atoms via shared molecule ids when available, or via minimum-image covalent distance otherwise. Pass NULL for all five output arrays to query n_waters.

```c
seams_status seams_water_vectors(const seams_system *sys, int oxygen_type, int hydrogen_type, int *mol_ids, double *oh_mid, double *bisector, double *hh, double *hh_unit, size_t cap, size_t *n_waters);
```

Parameters: `sys`, `oxygen_type`, `hydrogen_type`, `mol_ids`, `oh_mid`, `bisector`, `hh`, `hh_unit`, `cap`, `n_waters`.

- `sys`: Frame handle.
- `oxygen_type`: Species integer of water oxygen.
- `hydrogen_type`: Species integer of water hydrogen, distinct from oxygen_type.
- `mol_ids`: Receives molecule ids, length cap, or NULL.
- `oh_mid`: Receives O-to-H-midpoint vectors in Angstrom, 3 * cap doubles, or NULL.
- `bisector`: Receives unit bisector vectors, 3 * cap doubles, or NULL.
- `hh`: Receives H1-to-H2 vectors in Angstrom, 3 * cap doubles, or NULL.
- `hh_unit`: Receives unit H1-to-H2 vectors, 3 * cap doubles, or NULL.
- `cap`: Molecule capacity of every non-NULL output array.
- `n_waters`: Receives the water count.

Returns: SEAMS_OK; SEAMS_ERR_NULL; SEAMS_ERR_STATE; SEAMS_ERR_RANGE; SEAMS_ERR_ARG; SEAMS_ERR_BOX; SEAMS_ERR_NOMEM.

Ownership: The caller owns all output arrays.

Thread safety: Read-only on sys.

Units: as given for each parameter above.

Example:

```c
size_t nw = 0;
seams_water_vectors(sys, 1, 2, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, &nw);
```

The tour call is in `docs/examples/c_api_tour.c`.

Errors: SEAMS_ERR_NULL, SEAMS_ERR_RANGE, SEAMS_ERR_BOX, SEAMS_ERR_ARG, SEAMS_ERR_STATE, SEAMS_ERR_NOMEM, or SEAMS_ERR_INTERNAL. seams_last_error() holds the detail, and seams_handle_error(handle) when the call took a handle.

Example: `docs/examples/c_api_tour.c`

The program those lines come from:

```default
/* Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
 * Call every seams.h export on the in-tree fixtures and print one line each.
 * docs/check_c_api_tour.py requires those lines to appear in docs/api/c.md.
 */
#include "seams.h"

#include <math.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static void die(const char *what, seams_status status, const void *handle) {
  fprintf(stderr, "%s status %s last %s handle %s\n", what, seams_status_string(status),
          seams_last_error(), handle ? seams_handle_error(handle) : "");
  exit(1);
}

static void need(const char *what, seams_status status, const void *handle) {
  if (status != SEAMS_OK) {
    die(what, status, handle);
  }
}

static double mean_of(const double *values, int n) {
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += values[i];
  }
  return n > 0 ? sum / n : 0.0;
}

static int count_label(const int *labels, int n, int want) {
  int found = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    if (labels[i] == want) {
      ++found;
    }
  }
  return found;
}

static void diamond8(double *xyz, double *edge) {
  const double a = 2.75 * 4.0 / sqrt(3.0);
  const double fcc[4][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.5, 0.5, 0}, {0.5, 0, 0.5}, {0, 0.5, 0.5}};
  const double basis[2][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.25, 0.25, 0.25}};
  int n = 0;
  for (int f = 0; f < 4; ++f) {
    for (int s = 0; s < 2; ++s, ++n) {
      xyz[3 * n] = (fcc[f][0] + basis[s][0]) * a;
      xyz[3 * n + 1] = (fcc[f][1] + basis[s][1]) * a;
      xyz[3 * n + 2] = (fcc[f][2] + basis[s][2]) * a;
    }
  }
  *edge = a;
}

static seams_status tour_quench(const double *xyz, size_t n, const double *box9, size_t box_len,
                                double *xyz_out, size_t xyz_out_len, double *box9_out,
                                size_t box9_out_len, void *user_data) {
  (void)user_data;
  if (xyz == NULL || box9 == NULL || xyz_out == NULL || xyz_out_len < 3 * n || box_len != 9) {
    return SEAMS_ERR_NULL;
  }
  for (size_t i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    xyz_out[3 * i] = 25.0 * (double)i;
    xyz_out[3 * i + 1] = 0.0;
    xyz_out[3 * i + 2] = 0.0;
  }
  if (box9_out != NULL && box9_out_len == 9) {
    memcpy(box9_out, box9, sizeof(double) * 9);
  }
  return SEAMS_OK;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  const char *root = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : ".";
  char ice[512], si[512], tip[512];
  snprintf(ice, sizeof ice, "%s/input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", root);
  snprintf(si, sizeof si, "%s/input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj", root);
  snprintf(tip, sizeof tip, "%s/input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj", root);

  printf("capi seams_abi %d\n", seams_abi());
  printf("capi seams_version %d\n", seams_version());
  printf("capi seams_version_major %d\n", seams_version_major());
  printf("capi seams_version_minor %d\n", seams_version_minor());
  printf("capi seams_version_patch %d\n", seams_version_patch());
  printf("capi seams_version_string %s\n", seams_version_string());
  printf("capi seams_status_string %s\n", seams_status_string(SEAMS_OK));
  printf("capi seams_label_name %s\n", seams_label_name(SEAMS_LABEL_HEXAGONAL));
  printf("capi seams_ring_symmetry_name %s\n", seams_ring_symmetry_name(SEAMS_RING_HEXAGON));

  need("threads", seams_set_num_threads(1), NULL);
  printf("capi seams_set_num_threads %d\n", seams_get_num_threads());
  need("threads0", seams_set_num_threads(0), NULL);
  printf("capi seams_get_num_threads %d\n", seams_get_num_threads() > 0 ? 1 : 0);
  need("threads1", seams_set_num_threads(1), NULL);

  printf("capi seams_system_count %d\n", seams_system_count(NULL));
  seams_system *empty = seams_system_create();
  if (empty == NULL) {
    die("create", SEAMS_ERR_NOMEM, NULL);
  }
  printf("capi seams_system_create %d\n", empty != NULL);
  int scratch[8] = {0};
  seams_status bad = seams_chill_plus(empty, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED,
                                       scratch, NULL);
  printf("capi seams_last_error %s\n", seams_last_error());
  printf("capi seams_last_error_message %s\n", seams_last_error_message());
  printf("capi seams_handle_error %s\n",
         strstr(seams_handle_error(empty), "no frame") ? "no-frame" : "other");
  seams_system_destroy(empty);
  printf("capi seams_system_destroy ok\n");
  seams_system_destroy(NULL);
  seams_neighbours_destroy(NULL);
  printf("capi seams_neighbours_destroy ok\n");
  seams_rings_destroy(NULL);
  printf("capi seams_rings_destroy ok\n");
  seams_cages_destroy(NULL);
  printf("capi seams_cages_destroy ok\n");
  seams_brine_destroy(NULL);
  printf("capi seams_brine_destroy ok\n");
  seams_fingerprint_destroy(NULL);
  printf("capi seams_fingerprint_destroy ok\n");

  double xyz[24], edge = 0;
  diamond8(xyz, &edge);
  double box9[9] = {0, 0, 0, edge, edge, edge, 0, 0, 0};
  seams_system *cell = seams_system_create();
  need("set_atoms", seams_system_set_atoms(cell, xyz, 8, box9, 9, NULL, NULL), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_set_atoms %d\n", seams_system_count(cell));
  need("set_frame", seams_system_set_frame(cell, xyz, 8, box9, NULL, NULL), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_set_frame %d\n", seams_system_count(cell));
  need("set_ortho",
       seams_system_set_ortho(cell, xyz, 8, 0, 0, 0, edge, edge, edge, NULL, NULL), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_set_ortho %d\n", seams_system_count(cell));
  int labels8[8];
  int counts9[9];
  need("chill8",
       seams_chill_plus(cell, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels8, counts9),
       cell);
  printf("capi seams_chill_plus cubic %d\n", counts9[SEAMS_LABEL_CUBIC]);

  size_t nframes = 0;
  need("nframes", seams_path_nframes(ice, &nframes), NULL);
  printf("capi seams_path_nframes %zu\n", nframes);
  seams_system *ih = seams_system_create();
  need("read", seams_system_read(ih, ice, 1, 1), ih);
  const int n = seams_system_count(ih);
  printf("capi seams_system_read %d\n", n);
  size_t natoms = 0;
  need("natoms", seams_system_natoms(ih, &natoms), ih);
  printf("capi seams_system_natoms %zu\n", natoms);

  double moved[24];
  for (int k = 0; k < 24; ++k) {
    moved[k] = xyz[k] + 0.25;
  }
  need("set_positions", seams_system_set_positions(cell, moved, 8, NULL, 0), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_set_positions %d\n", seams_system_count(cell));
  need("stage_positions", seams_system_stage_positions(cell, 1), cell);
  need("set_positions", seams_system_set_positions(cell, moved, 8, NULL, 0), cell);
  need("stage_positions", seams_system_stage_positions(cell, 0), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_stage_positions %d\n", seams_system_count(cell));
  double cell9[9];
  need("box", seams_system_box(cell, cell9, 9), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_box %.3f %.3f %.3f %.3f %.3f %.3f\n", cell9[0], cell9[1], cell9[2],
         cell9[3], cell9[4], cell9[5]);
  double back[24];
  need("positions", seams_system_positions(cell, back, 24), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_positions %.3f %.3f %.3f\n", back[0], back[1], back[2]);
  int types8[8];
  need("types", seams_system_types(cell, types8, 8), cell);
  int ones = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < 8; ++i) {
    ones += types8[i] == 1;
  }
  printf("capi seams_system_types %d of type 1\n", ones);
  int ids8[8];
  need("ids", seams_system_ids(cell, ids8, 8), cell);
  printf("capi seams_system_ids %d %d\n", ids8[0], ids8[7]);

  seams_neighbours *nb = NULL;
  need("neigh", seams_neighbours_build(ih, 3.5, 1, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, &nb), ih);
  printf("capi seams_neighbours_build %d\n", seams_neighbours_count(nb));
  printf("capi seams_neighbours_count %d\n", seams_neighbours_count(nb));
  size_t rows = 0;
  need("nrows", seams_neighbours_nrows(nb, &rows), nb);
  printf("capi seams_neighbours_nrows %zu\n", rows);
  size_t n_off = 0, nnz = 0;
  need("copyq", seams_neighbours_copy(nb, NULL, 0, &n_off, NULL, 0, &nnz), nb);
  int *offsets = calloc(n_off, sizeof(int));
  int *cols = calloc(nnz ? nnz : 1, sizeof(int));
  need("copy", seams_neighbours_copy(nb, offsets, n_off, &n_off, cols, nnz, &nnz), nb);
  printf("capi seams_neighbours_copy %zu %zu\n", n_off, nnz);

  need("msdq", seams_msd_curve(msd, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, &msd_lags), msd);
  printf("capi seams_msd_curve %zu\n", msd_lags);
  double dtot = 0, dax = 0, dlat = 0, malpha = 0;
  need("msdf", seams_msd_fit(msd, 0.0, 0.0, &dtot, &dax, &dlat, &malpha), msd);
  printf("capi seams_msd_fit %.1f\n", malpha);
  seams_msd_destroy(msd);
  printf("capi seams_msd_destroy ok\n");

  seams_hbond_tcf *hbt = NULL;
  need("hbtc", seams_hbond_tcf_create(4, 1, 1.0, 1, &hbt), NULL);
  printf("capi seams_hbond_tcf_create ok\n");
  const int hd[2] = {1, 2}, ha[2] = {3, 4};
  need("hbtp0", seams_hbond_tcf_push(hbt, hd, ha, 2), hbt);
  need("hbtp1", seams_hbond_tcf_push(hbt, hd, ha, 1), hbt);
  printf("capi seams_hbond_tcf_push 2\n");
  size_t hbt_lags = 0;
  need("hbtq", seams_hbond_tcf_curve(hbt, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, &hbt_lags), hbt);
  printf("capi seams_hbond_tcf_curve %zu\n", hbt_lags);
  double tci = 0, tsi = 0;
  need("hbtf", seams_hbond_tcf_fit(hbt, 0.0, 0.0, &tci, NULL, &tsi, NULL), hbt);
  printf("capi seams_hbond_tcf_fit %.2f %.2f\n", tci, tsi);
  seams_hbond_tcf_destroy(hbt);
  printf("capi seams_hbond_tcf_destroy ok\n");

  seams_reorient *rot = NULL;
  need("rotc", seams_reorient_create(1, 4, 1, 1.0, &rot), NULL);
  printf("capi seams_reorient_create ok\n");
  const double rv0[3] = {0, 0, 1}, rv1[3] = {0.6, 0, 0.8};
  need("rotp0", seams_reorient_push(rot, rv0, 1), rot);
  need("rotp1", seams_reorient_push(rot, rv1, 1), rot);
  printf("capi seams_reorient_push 2\n");
  size_t rot_lags = 0;
  need("rotq", seams_reorient_curve(rot, NULL, NULL, NULL, NULL, 0, &rot_lags), rot);
  printf("capi seams_reorient_curve %zu\n", rot_lags);
  double r1i = 0, r2i = 0;
  need("rotf", seams_reorient_fit(rot, 0.0, 0.0, &r1i, NULL, &r2i, NULL), rot);
  printf("capi seams_reorient_fit %.2f %.2f\n", r1i, r2i);
  seams_reorient_destroy(rot);
  printf("capi seams_reorient_destroy ok\n");

  free(mix_mols);
  free(wbis);

  seams_rings_destroy(rings);
  seams_neighbours_destroy(nb);
  seams_neighbours_destroy(knn);
  seams_system_destroy(cell);
  seams_system_destroy(ih);
  seams_system_destroy(guest);
  seams_system_destroy(mix);
  seams_system_destroy(pore);
  free(offsets);
  free(cols);
  free(labels);
  free(q4);
  free(q6);
  free(q6bar);
  free(sizes);
  free(sym);
  free(verts);
  free(per);
  free(shell);
  free(ice_flag);
  free(rr);
  free(gg);
  free(rc);
  free(cnr);
  free(cnv);
  free(edges);
  free(raw_labels);
  free(q_labels);
  free(zz);
  free(rho);
  free(key);
  free(kinds);
  return 0;
}
```

# C++ {#c}

`include/seams.hpp` is the header-only C++ API. It lives in namespace
`seams`, includes `seams.h`, and links `libseams`. Meson installs the
header next to `seams.h`. `pkg-config --cflags seams` and
`find_package(seams)` both put that directory on the include path.
`SEAMS_CXX_HEADER` in `seams-config.cmake` is the installed `seams.hpp`.

## Quickstart {#quickstart}

```bash
c++ -std=c++20 -Iinclude docs/examples/cpp_api.cpp -Lbuild/src -lseams -o cpp_api
./cpp_api "$PWD"
```

The eight-atom diamond is cubic. Ice Ih is hexagonal, 128 atoms, with mean
q6-bar 0.562448843702.

```cpp
/* Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
 * Idiomatic seams.hpp on the eight-atom diamond and on ice Ih.
 */
#include "seams.hpp"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace {

std::vector<double> diamond8(double &edge) {
  const double a = 2.75 * 4.0 / std::sqrt(3.0);
  const double fcc[4][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.5, 0.5, 0}, {0.5, 0, 0.5}, {0, 0.5, 0.5}};
  const double basis[2][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.25, 0.25, 0.25}};
  std::vector<double> xyz;
  xyz.reserve(24);
  for (const auto &shift : fcc) {
    for (const auto &site : basis) {
      xyz.push_back((shift[0] + site[0]) * a);
      xyz.push_back((shift[1] + site[1]) * a);
      xyz.push_back((shift[2] + site[2]) * a);
    }
  }
  edge = a;
  return xyz;
}

}  // namespace

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  try {
    seams::set_num_threads(1);
    if (seams::num_threads() != 1 || seams::version().empty()) {
      return 1;
    }
    double edge = 0;
    const auto xyz = diamond8(edge);
    seams::System cell;
    cell.set_ortho(xyz, edge, edge, edge);
    const auto cubic = cell.chill_plus(seams::ChillOptions{});
    const auto orders = cell.q4q6(3.5);
    double mean = 0;
    for (double value : orders.q6) {
      mean += value;
    }
    mean /= static_cast<double>(orders.q6.size());
    if (cubic.counts[0] != 8 || !(mean > 0.3)) {
      return 1;
    }
    std::printf("cpp api cubic %d q6 %.3f %s\n", cubic.counts[0], mean, seams::version().c_str());
    if (argc < 2) {
      return 0;
    }
    seams::System ice;
    ice.read(std::string(argv[1]) + "/input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", 1, -1);
    const auto labels = ice.chill_plus(seams::ChillOptions{});
    const auto q6 = ice.q6bar(seams::Q6BarOptions{});
    const auto shell = ice.symmetry(0.0);
    int n_ih = 0;
    for (int label : shell) {
      n_ih += label == 0 ? 1 : 0;
    }
    std::vector<int> flags(static_cast<std::size_t>(ice.count()), 1);
    const auto front = ice.brine(flags, seams::BrineOptions{});
    const auto pockets = front.pockets();
    std::printf("ice Ih atoms %d hexagonal %d q6bar %.12f shell_ih %d pockets %d\n", ice.count(),
                labels.counts[static_cast<std::size_t>(static_cast<int>(seams::Label::Hexagonal))],
                q6.mean, n_ih, pockets.pockets);
    if (ice.count() != 128 || labels.counts[1] != 128) {
      return 1;
    }
    if (std::abs(q6.mean - 0.562448843702) > 1e-9) {
      return 1;
    }
  } catch (const seams::Error &err) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "seams::Error %d %s\n", err.code(), err.what());
    return 1;
  }
  return 0;
}
```

The wider language ABI remains `libseams_lang` (`seams_frame_*`). A program
that only needs `seams.hpp` does not link it. `docs/examples/minimal_cpp.cpp`
is that ABI on the GenIce sI cell.

```cpp
/** Null when path is null or the file cannot be read.
 * seams_last_error() then names the reason. @ingroup lang_frame */
seams_frame *seams_frame_read(const char *path, int frame, int type_filter);
/** Read with chemfiles name filters and type assignments. options may be
 * null, which is identical to seams_frame_read. @ingroup lang_frame */
seams_frame *seams_frame_read_options(
    const char *path, int frame, int type_filter,
    const seams_chemfiles_load_options *options);
```

Its frame-mutation and order-parameter entries are
`seams_frame_set_positions`, `seams_frame_steinhardt_graph`,
`seams_frame_wl`, `seams_frame_q4_q6`, and
`seams_frame_q4_q6_chill`.

```cpp
/** Replace coordinates of a frame built by seams_frame_from_arrays.
 * n must be the atom count already stored. The box is nine LAMMPS numbers. @ingroup lang_frame */
int seams_frame_set_positions(seams_frame *frame, const double *xyz, int n,
                             const double *box9);

/** Phase times are seconds. reused is 1 when the wide neighbour list was
 * kept from an earlier call. A null times pointer skips the record. */
typedef struct seams_phase_times {
  double neighbours;
  double chill;
  double rings;
  int reused;
} seams_phase_times;

/** CHILL+ and primitive rings on one neighbour list.
 * skin > 0 builds that list at cutoff+skin and keeps it while every atom's
 * minimum-image displacement stays within skin/2. Bonds are the pairs
 * still inside cutoff, so the labels match a fresh cutoff list.
 * skin <= 0 builds a fresh cutoff list on every call. */
/** @ingroup lang_rings */
int seams_frame_chill_rings(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int type,
                           const char *graph, int max_ring, double skin,
                           int *labels, int counts9[9], int *ring_counts,
                           int ring_counts_len, seams_phase_times *times);

/** Build the cutoff neighbour list and discard it. graph NULL means cutoff.
 * seams_frame_neighbour_pairs then returns the directed pairs of that list. @ingroup lang_order */
int seams_frame_neighbours(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int type,
                           const char *graph);
/** @brief seams_frame_neighbour_pairs. @ingroup lang_order */
int seams_frame_neighbour_pairs(const seams_frame *frame);

/** H-bond edge export. Rows are sorted by (donor, acceptor, hydrogen).
 * donor and acceptor are frame indices. hydrogen is UINT32_MAX when
 * SEAMS_HBOND_EDGE_WITH_H is not requested. fields is the same bitmask as
 * seams_hbond_edges in seams.h. Any non-null output column needs cap rows.
 * n_out receives the edge count. */
int seams_frame_hbond_edges(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int oxygen_type,
                            int hydrogen_type, double dist_cutoff,
                            double angle_cutoff, int fields, uint32_t *donor,
                            uint32_t *acceptor, uint32_t *hydrogen,
                            double *d_DA, double *angle, int cap, int *n_out);

/** Local Steinhardt q_l on the cutoff shell. A null qlbar skips the
 * Lechner-Dellago average; the local values do not use that pass.
 * An empty shell is 0: the harmonic row stays zero and is not divided
 * by the neighbour count. freud and pyscal3 store NaN for that atom. */
/** @ingroup lang_order */
int seams_frame_steinhardt(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int type,
                           int order_l, double *ql, double *qlbar);
/** graph is "mutual" (four nearest, the historical default) or "cutoff"
 * (the orthoFullCsr list, the same neighbours as `seams steinhardt`). @ingroup lang_order */
int seams_frame_steinhardt_graph(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int type,
                                 int order_l, const char *graph, double *ql,
                                 double *qlbar);

/** Normalized Steinhardt hat{w}_l for l = 4 or 6 on the cutoff shell.
 * Returns 1 on failure. @ingroup lang_order */
int seams_frame_wl(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int type, int order_l,
                   double *wl);

/** Local q4 and q6 on the cutoff shell. Degrees 4 and 6 use the
 * solid-harmonic kernel. q4bar and q6bar may be null, and a null
 * pointer skips that Lechner-Dellago average. An empty shell is 0
 * for both the local value and the average. Returns 1 on failure. */
/** @ingroup lang_order */
int seams_frame_q4_q6(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int type, double *q4,
                      double *q6, double *q4bar, double *q6bar);

/** One cutoff list. Local q4, local q6, Lechner-Dellago q4-bar and
 * q6-bar, and published CHILL+ labels. q4bar and q6bar may be null.
 * counts9 and labels may be null. Returns 1 on failure. @ingroup lang_order */
int seams_frame_q4_q6_chill(seams_frame *frame, double cutoff, int type,
                            double *q4, double *q6, double *q4bar,
                            double *q6bar, int *labels, int counts9[9]);
```

`docs/examples/core_counts.cpp` is the same census on Ice Ih and sII.

```cpp
// Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
/* Same Ice Ih and sII census as core_counts.c, through seams.h. */
#include "seams.h"
#include "seams_lammps_box.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <cstring>
#include <vector>

static int read_dump(const char *path, std::vector<double> &xyz, std::vector<int> &types,
                     double box9[9]) {
  FILE *in = std::fopen(path, "r");
  char line[512];
  int reading = 0;
  if (in == nullptr) {
    return 1;
  }
  while (std::fgets(line, sizeof line, in) != nullptr) {
    if (std::strncmp(line, "ITEM: BOX BOUNDS", 16) == 0) {
      double bound_lo[3], bound_hi[3], tilt[3];
      for (int axis = 0; axis < 3; ++axis) {
        char bound[128];
        if (std::fgets(bound, sizeof bound, in) == nullptr) {
          std::fclose(in);
          return 1;
        }
        tilt[axis] = 0.0;
        if (std::sscanf(bound, "%lf %lf %lf", &bound_lo[axis], &bound_hi[axis], &tilt[axis]) < 2) {
          std::fclose(in);
          return 1;
        }
      }
      seams_lammps_bounds(bound_lo, bound_hi, tilt, box9);
    } else if (std::strncmp(line, "ITEM: ATOMS", 11) == 0) {
      reading = 1;
    } else if (reading) {
      int id, kind;
      double x, y, z;
      if (std::sscanf(line, "%d %d %lf %lf %lf", &id, &kind, &x, &y, &z) != 5) {
        break;
      }
      types.push_back(kind);
      xyz.push_back(x);
      xyz.push_back(y);
      xyz.push_back(z);
    }
  }
  std::fclose(in);
  return xyz.empty() ? 1 : 0;
}

static int classify(const char *path, int &n, int counts[9], int rings[13]) {
  std::vector<double> xyz;
  std::vector<int> types;
  double box9[9] = {};
  if (read_dump(path, xyz, types, box9) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  n = static_cast<int>(types.size());
  std::vector<int> labels(static_cast<size_t>(n));
  seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
  seams_rings *found = nullptr;
  if (sys == nullptr ||
      seams_system_set_frame(sys, xyz.data(), n, box9, types.data(), nullptr) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels.data(),
                       counts) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_rings_find(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, 6, &found) != SEAMS_OK ||
      seams_rings_histogram(found, rings, 13) != SEAMS_OK) {
    if (found != nullptr) {
      seams_rings_destroy(found);
    }
    if (sys != nullptr) {
      seams_system_destroy(sys);
    }
    return 1;
  }
  seams_rings_destroy(found);
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  return 0;
}

int main() {
  int n = 0;
  int counts[9] = {};
  int rings[13] = {};
  if (seams_set_num_threads(1) != SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (classify("input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj", n, counts, rings) != 0 || n != 128 ||
      counts[1] != 128 || rings[6] != 256) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "ice Ih n=%d hexagonal=%d rings6=%d\n", n, counts[1], rings[6]);
    return 1;
  }
  if (classify("input/traj/genice_sII.lammpstrj", n, counts, rings) != 0 || n != 136 ||
      counts[4] != 136 || rings[5] != 144 || rings[6] != 16) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "sII n=%d clathrate=%d rings5=%d rings6=%d\n", n, counts[4], rings[5],
                 rings[6]);
    return 1;
  }
  std::printf("cpp hexagonal 128 rings6 256 clathrate 136 rings5 144\n");
  return 0;
}
```

```cpp
// Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
/* Read the GenIce sI cell through the C++ language header. */
#include "seams_lang.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <vector>

int main(int argc, char **argv) {
  const char *path = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj";
  seams_frame *frame = seams_frame_read(path, 1, 0);
  if (frame == nullptr || seams_frame_nop(frame) != 46) {
    std::fprintf(stderr, "%s\n", seams_last_error());
    return 1;
  }
  if (seams_frame_neighbours(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff") != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (seams_frame_neighbour_pairs(frame) < 150) {
    return 1;
  }
  double q6[46];
  if (seams_frame_steinhardt(frame, 3.5, 0, 6, q6, nullptr) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  double mean = 0;
  for (double value : q6) {
    mean += value;
  }
  mean /= 46.0;
  int labels[46];
  int counts[9];
  if (seams_frame_chill_plus(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", labels, counts) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  int rings[7] = {};
  if (seams_frame_rings(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", 6, rings, 7) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  int n_five = 0;
  int per_atom[46];
  if (seams_frame_chordless(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", 5, nullptr, 0, &n_five, per_atom) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  int five[48 * 5];
  if (n_five != 48 ||
      seams_frame_chordless(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", 5, five, 48 * 5, &n_five, nullptr) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  int through = 0;
  for (int n : per_atom) {
    through += n;
  }
  if (through != 5 * 48 || five[0] != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  int n_cages = 0;
  int n_sig_atoms = 0;
  int n_vertices = 0;
  if (seams_frame_signature(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", "512", &n_cages, &n_sig_atoms) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  int n_edge = 0;
  int n_edge_atoms = 0;
  if (seams_frame_signature_edge(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", "512", "none", &n_edge,
                                 &n_edge_atoms) != 0 ||
      n_edge != n_cages) {
    return 1;
  }
  int n_tight = 0;
  int n_tight_atoms = 0;
  if (seams_frame_signature_edge(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", "512", "1,2", &n_tight,
                                 &n_tight_atoms) != 0 ||
      n_tight != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (n_cages > 0 &&
      seams_frame_signature_vertices(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", "512", 0, nullptr, 0,
                                     &n_vertices) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (n_cages > 0 &&
      seams_frame_signature_vertices_edge(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", "512", "none", 0, nullptr, 0,
                                          &n_vertices) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  // CHILL+ and rings from one neighbour list, with the phase times.
  int fused[9] = {};
  int fused_rings[7] = {};
  seams_phase_times times{};
  if (seams_frame_chill_rings(frame, 3.5, 0, "cutoff", 6, 0.0, labels, fused, fused_rings, 7,
                              &times) != 0 ||
      fused[4] != counts[4]) {
    return 1;
  }
  int shell[46];
  if (seams_frame_symmetry(frame, 0.12, shell) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (seams_frame_rdf_nbins(6.0, 0) < 1) {
    return 1;
  }
  const int n_r2 = seams_frame_rdf2d_nbin(3.5, 0.5);
  std::vector<double> r2(static_cast<std::size_t>(n_r2));
  std::vector<double> g2(static_cast<std::size_t>(n_r2));
  if (seams_frame_rdf2d(frame, 3.5, 0.5, nullptr, r2.data(), g2.data()) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  int sheet[8] = {};
  if (seams_frame_monolayer(frame, 3.5, 0, 6, 1.0, nullptr, sheet, 8) != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  // The same positions as a new frame with one molecule per atom.
  double box9[9];
  seams_frame_box(frame, box9);
  std::vector<int> types(46, 1);
  std::vector<int> mols(46);
  for (int i = 0; i < 46; ++i) {
    mols[static_cast<std::size_t>(i)] = i + 1;
  }
  seams_frame *copy = seams_frame_from_species(seams_frame_positions(frame), 46, box9,
                                               types.data(), nullptr, mols.data());
  if (copy == nullptr) {
    return 1;
  }
  double tau = 0.0;
  const int jump = seams_frames_jump_tau90(frame, copy, 1.0, 1, 2, &tau);
  seams_frame_free(copy);
  if (jump != 0) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (counts[4] != 46 || rings[5] != 48 || rings[6] != 54 || mean <= 0.5) {
    return 1;
  }
  std::printf("%s atoms 46 clathrate %d q6 %.3f rings %d\n", seams_lang_version(), counts[4],
              mean, rings[5] + rings[6]);
  const double heavy_hb[] = {0, 0, 0, 2.8, 0, 0};
  const double hyd_hb[] = {1, 0, 0};
  const int heavy_type_hb[] = {8, 8};
  const int heavy_mol_hb[] = {1, 2};
  const int hyd_type_hb[] = {2};
  const int hyd_mol_hb[] = {1};
  const double cell_hb[] = {0, 0, 0, 20, 20, 20, 0, 0, 0};
  const int donor_hb[] = {8};
  seams_frame *hb = seams_frame_from_hydrogen_cloud(
      heavy_hb, 2, heavy_type_hb, nullptr, heavy_mol_hb, hyd_hb, 1, hyd_type_hb, nullptr,
      hyd_mol_hb, cell_hb);
  int n_hb = 0;
  if (hb == nullptr ||
      seams_frame_directed_hbonds(hb, 3.5, 2.42, 30.0, donor_hb, 1, donor_hb, 1, 2, 1, nullptr,
                                  nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, 0, &n_hb) != 0 ||
      n_hb != 1) {
    seams_frame_free(hb);
    return 1;
  }
  seams_frame_free(hb);
  seams_frame_free(frame);
  return 0;
}
```

`docs/examples/ice.cpp` is the eight-atom C call.

```cpp
// Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
#include "seams.h"

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdio>

int main() {
  const double a = 2.75 * 4.0 / std::sqrt(3.0);
  const double fcc[4][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.5, 0.5, 0}, {0.5, 0, 0.5}, {0, 0.5, 0.5}};
  const double basis[2][3] = {{0, 0, 0}, {0.25, 0.25, 0.25}};
  double xyz[24];
  int n = 0;
  for (int f = 0; f < 4; f++) {
    for (int s = 0; s < 2; s++, n++) {
      xyz[3 * n] = (fcc[f][0] + basis[s][0]) * a;
      xyz[3 * n + 1] = (fcc[f][1] + basis[s][1]) * a;
      xyz[3 * n + 2] = (fcc[f][2] + basis[s][2]) * a;
    }
  }
  if (seams_set_num_threads(1) != SEAMS_OK || seams_get_num_threads() != 1) {
    return 1;
  }
  int labels[8];
  int counts[9];
  double q4[8];
  double q6[8];
  seams_system *sys = seams_system_create();
  if (seams_system_set_ortho(sys, xyz, 8, 0, 0, 0, a, a, a, nullptr, nullptr) != SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (seams_chill_plus(sys, 3.5, 0, SEAMS_GRAPH_CUTOFF, SEAMS_CHILL_PUBLISHED, labels, counts) !=
      SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  if (seams_q4q6(sys, 3.5, 0, q4, q6) != SEAMS_OK) {
    return 1;
  }
  double mean = 0;
  for (double value : q6) {
    mean += value;
  }
  mean /= 8.0;
  std::printf("%s cubic %d q6 %.3f\n", seams_version_string(), counts[0], mean);
  seams_system_destroy(sys);
  return counts[0] == 8 && mean > 0.3 ? 0 : 1;
}
```

## Concepts {#concepts}

`System`, `Neighbours`, `Rings`, `Cages`, `Fingerprint`, and `Brine` are
move-only. The destructor frees the C handle. Copying is deleted.

A status other than success throws `seams::Error`. `what()` is
`seams_handle_error`. `code()` is the status integer. `status()` is the
`Status` enumerator.

Coordinates enter as `std::span<const double>`. Paths and site-table text
enter as `std::string_view`. Results come back as values, `std::vector`,
`std::array`, or `std::string`. `Neighbours::pairs` returns the directed
pairs. `Rings` is a range: `begin` and `end` walk the rings.

`Graph`, `ChillRule`, `Label`, `CageLabel`, `SiteKind`, `RingSymmetry`,
`Axis`, and `DomainSubset` are `enum class`. Analyses with several knobs
take an options aggregate. `ChillOptions`, `SteinhardtOptions`,
`CageOptions`, `DistributionOptions`, `BondOptions`, and the rest default
to the published cutoff of 3.5 angstroms.

Methods that return a value are `[[nodiscard]]`. A method that reads a
frame takes a non-const `System` because the C call clears the handle
error. `count` is const.

A handle requires exclusive use. Two frames on two threads may run
`steinhardt`, `ql`, `q4q6`, or `q6bar` at the same time; the Steinhardt
scratch inside the library belongs to the calling thread. `set_num_threads`
is process-global.

Doxygen comments on `seams.hpp` and `seams.h` are the C++ reference at
`api/index`.

## Ice Ih {#ice-ih}

`input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj`, frame 1, every atom, cutoff 3.5 angstrom, one
thread. These numbers are the C++ engine on that frame.

```default
ih n 128
ih chill0 0 128 0 0 0 0 0 0 0
ih q3 0.744029547233
ih q4 0.509334928671
ih q6 0.625855471508
ih q6bar 0.562448843702
ih q8 0.229702115021
ih q12 0.421988011385
ih vert 6 0
ih cages 128 0 0 0
ih knn 512
ih rdf 8 4158.664606579 0
ih rcn 26.204724409449
ih cn 4.031496062992
ih hbond 0
ih rho 4 0.030779111111
ih fp 16 256
ih site 8
ih pairs 0 128 0
ih domain 0 0 0
ih prism 0
ih sheet 256
```

`chill0` is the nine original CHILL populations in label order. q3 through
q12 are means. q6bar is the mean of the Lechner-Dellago average. `vert` is
the length of ring 0 and its first atom. `cages` is hexagonal, cubic,
water, both. `knn` is the mutual four-neighbour pair count. `rdf` is the
bin count, the volume in cubic angstroms, and g of the first bin. `rcn` is
the last running coordination. `cn` is the coordination to 3.5 angstroms.
`fp` is the fingerprint key length and the ring-census sum. `site` is atom
0 under `1=waterO`. `pairs` is contacts, cations, and anions under
`1=cationHead`. `domain` is the apolar subset. `prism` is perfect
six-stacks. `sheet` is six-rings in the monolayer histogram.

sI has 46 atoms and 2 cages of signature `512` covering 40 atoms. The XYZ
file has 256 atoms and coordination 43.325490196078 out to 6 angstroms.
The CON file has 4 atoms and 0 hydrogen bonds. Triclinic sH has 136 atoms
and mean q6 0.625601998379.

`symmetry` writes one shell label per atom. `brine` measures a planar front
from an ice flag per atom. `docs/examples/cpp_api.cpp` prints:

```default
ice Ih atoms 128 hexagonal 128 q6bar 0.562448843702 shell_ih 128 pockets 0
```

The test rejects any other hexagonal count or q6-bar mean.

## Errors and ownership {#errors-and-ownership}

```cpp
try {
  seams::System system;
  system.read("missing.lammpstrj", 1, -1);
} catch (const seams::Error &err) {
  // err.what() is seams_handle_error. err.code() is the status.
}
```

`System` and the result handles are move-only. A move leaves the source
empty. The destructor of an empty handle does nothing. The caller does not
call `seams_*_destroy`.

`bindings/cxx/test_lang.cpp` calls `libseams_lang`. That ABI is separate
from `seams.hpp`.

```cpp
    seams_phase_times times{};
    if (seams_frame_chill_rings(fresh, 3.5, 2, "cutoff", 6, 0.0, iceLabels.data(), fused,
                               ringCounts.data(), 9, &times) != 0) {

      return fail("chill rings");
    }
```

## Symbol reference {#symbol-reference}

### seams_frame {#seams-frame}

Purpose: Opaque frame used by the language bindings.

Parameters: none

Returns: The type itself.

Ownership: No allocation. This is a type.

Errors: None.

# Python {#python}

`pydseamslib` provides `import dseams` and `import pydseams`.

| name | role | library |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dseams | array calls | libseams (include/seams.h) |
| pydseams | Frame API | libseams and libseams_lang (bindings/cxx/seams_lang.h) |

The package and its symbol list are [d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib). The rendered reference is [PydSEAMSlib](https://d-seams.github.io/PydSEAMSlib/).

```bash
pip install pydseamslib
```

`dseams.chill_plus(coordinates, box)` returns one label per atom and nine counts. Index 0 is cubic and index 1 is hexagonal. On the eight-molecule cubic cell in the quickstart, index 0 is 8. On `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` (128 oxygens, LAMMPS type 1) the same call returns 128 at index 1, and the CLI prints:

```default
nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073
nop 128 hexagonal 128
```

The first classification is the [Python tutorial](../fronts/python.md).

# Fortran {#fortran}

The Fortran binding is the fpm Git dependency `dseams` in [d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran).

| module | role |
| --- | --- |
| seams | the module programs call |
| seams_c | iso_c_binding image of include/seams.h |

The package links an installed `libseams`. Kinds are `seams_real` (`real64`) and `seams_int` (`int32`). Coordinates have shape `(3, n)`.

```toml
[dependencies]
dseams = { git = "https://github.com/d-SEAMS/dseams-fortran" }
```

Programs call the `seams` module, which links an installed `libseams`. Coordinates have shape `(3, n)`. On `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` (128 oxygens, type 1) published CHILL+ at 3.5 angstrom is 128 hexagonal:

```default
nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073
nop 128 hexagonal 128
```

The first classification is the [Fortran tutorial](../fronts/fortran.md).

# Lua and Fennel {#lua-and-fennel}

The Lua and Fennel library is [d-SEAMS/yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct). `require("dseams")` in Lua and `(require :dseams)` in Fennel call `libseams` (`include/seams.h`). `require("yoda")` resolves to the same module.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct.git
cd yodaStruct
luarocks make
```

Option tables and return values are the [Lua reference](https://d-seams.github.io/yodaStruct/reference/lua.md).

`require("dseams")` and `(require :dseams)` call the same engine as the CLI. On `input/traj/ice1h.lammpstrj` (128 oxygens, type 1) published CHILL+ at 3.5 angstrom is 128 hexagonal:

```default
nop 128 frame 1 box 15.6457 14.7071 18.073
nop 128 hexagonal 128
```

The first classification is the [Lua and Fennel tutorial](../fronts/lua.md).

# Command line {#command-line}

`seams` reads a trajectory and prints one result. The cell in this example is `input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj`, 46 oxygens in a cube of edge 12.0034886 Å.

```bash
seams read input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj
seams cn input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
seams steinhardt input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --l 6
seams chill-plus input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
seams rings input/traj/genice_sI.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5
```

`read` prints the atom count and the box. `cn` is the cutoff coordination. `steinhardt` prints the mean local q6. `chill-plus` prints the label census. `rings` prints the primitive-ring histogram. On this cell the five commands print:

```default
nop 46 frame 1 box 12.0035 12.0035 12.0035
# site-site
# types 1 1 cutoff 3.5 cn 4.08889 nI 46 nJ 46 volume 1729.51
nop 46 q6 0.595133 q6bar 0.311125
nop 46 clathrate 46
nop 46 rings 102
5 48
6 54
```

`docs/examples/minimal_cli.sh` runs those five commands and checks for `nop 46`, `nI 46`, `q6 0.595`, `clathrate 46`, and `6 54`.

```bash
#!/bin/sh
# Copyright (c) d-SEAMS developers
# Read the GenIce sI cell with the seams CLI.
# Usage: minimal_cli.sh SEAMS FIXTURE
set -eu
SEAMS=$1
FIXTURE=$2
NO_COLOR=1 "$SEAMS" read "$FIXTURE" | grep -q "nop 46"
NO_COLOR=1 "$SEAMS" cn "$FIXTURE" --cutoff 3.5 | grep -q "nI 46"
NO_COLOR=1 "$SEAMS" steinhardt "$FIXTURE" --cutoff 3.5 --l 6 | grep -q "q6 0.595"
NO_COLOR=1 "$SEAMS" chill-plus "$FIXTURE" --cutoff 3.5 | grep -q "clathrate 46"
NO_COLOR=1 "$SEAMS" rings "$FIXTURE" --cutoff 3.5 | grep -q "^6 54"
echo "cli example ok"
```

# Science front {#science-front}

`src/include/internal/science_front.hpp` is the C++ layer profile and the single-trajectory critical size. The header is not installed and the functions are not in `seams.h`. `science-front`, from `scripts/science_front.cpp`, is the driver built with the engine.

The cutoff is `science::kCutoffA`, 3.5 Å. `science::kQ6BarIceCut` is 0.36. Neither value is fitted. CHILL+ is the published Nguyen and Molinero rule: q3 over the four nearest neighbours, a crystal row of four neighbours inside the cutoff, and the interfacial neighbour test. The OVITO rule is a separate label. It does not choose these labels. The shell label is 0 hexagonal, 1 cubic, 2 stacking-disordered, and -1 otherwise. q6-bar is the Lechner-Dellago average on the same cutoff.

## Layers {#layers}

`science::layersOf(cloud, axis, binWidth)` bins CHILL+, the shell label, q6 and q6-bar along one box edge. `axis` is 0, 1 or 2. A negative axis uses the longest edge. The default bin width is 1 Å. Empty bins between ice planes are filled before the front is fit. `Layers::n` is the number of molecules. `Layers::rows` is one `LayerRow` per bin: the bin center, the occupancy, the cubic, hexagonal, interfacial and liquid counts, the shell counts, and the mean q6 and q6-bar.

`science::fitSolidFraction(phi, mid, span)` turns a binned solid fraction into the 10-90 fronts. `Front::position` is the 0.5 crossing. `Front::width` is the 10-90 width of that crossing. A flat crystal, with no fall through 0.5, leaves `Layers::defined` false and the front list empty.

`science::bootstrapSlope(x, y, nDraw, seed)` is the ordinary-least-squares slope and a percentile bootstrap. A draw whose x values have no spread is dropped. The driver uses it for the two front positions and for the ice thickness. Half the thickness slope is the mean advance of the two fronts when the slab grows from both sides.

## One frame {#one-frame}

`science::nucleusOf(cloud, frame, q6Cut)` labels one frame and leaves the published CHILL+ label on the cloud. `NucleusFrame` holds the CHILL+ census, the shell census, the q6-bar ice count and mean, the stacking molecules split by the CHILL+ label, and the polytype agreement. `core`, `extended`, `shell` and `q6` are the largest clusters. The extended cluster is cubic, hexagonal and interfacial. The core cluster is cubic and hexagonal.

`science::labelAtoms(cloud, q6Cut)` returns one `AtomRow` per molecule: coordinates, the published CHILL+ label, the OVITO CHILL+ label, the shell label, q6, q6-bar, and whether the molecule is in the extended cluster.

## Critical size {#critical-size}

`science::criticalSize(series, nDraw, seed)` reads the largest-cluster size at each frame. The critical size is the mean of the contiguous band around the smallest value. The band stops where the size exceeds that minimum by the larger of 5 molecules and 15 percent. `nStar` is that mean. `lo` and `hi` are a percentile bootstrap of the mean. `onset` is the frame of the minimum. `window` is the width of the band.

This is an upper bound, not a committor. A minimum in the first two frames, followed by a larger cluster, sets `upperBound`. The dump starts after the nucleus is already at least that large. The number is not the probability that the cluster will grow.

# Changelog {#changelog}

Release notes for the d-SEAMS engine. This repository builds
`libyodaLib`, the C library `libseams` (`include/seams.h`), the
language ABI `libseams_lang`, and the `seams` command. Each language
binding is its own package. See the
[2.14 release notes](../reference/release-2.14.md) for changes in
all 2.14 releases. The overview below covers the 2.14.0 ABI and package split.

## 2.14.0 {#id1}

`seams.h` is ABI 1. Callers moving from
2.13 follow the [upgrade guide](../user/howto/upgrade-2.14.md).

### Highlights {#highlights}

- A frame carries an orthorhombic or triclinic cell. The C API returns
  neighbours, the published CHILL+ rule and the OVITO rule, q4 and q6,
  primitive rings, and ring symmetry labels.
- CHILL+ defaults to the cutoff neighbour list. `--graph mutual` is the
  mutual four-nearest list.
- LAMMPS, GROMACS, and OpenMM call the library on the frames a running
  calculation chooses. The report is the primitive ring census, the
  published CHILL labels, and the hexagonal and double-diamond cage
  flags.
- The ice label is the scale-free residual of the seventeen-atom shell
  after the optimal rotation and scale. The shell is the central atom,
  its four bonded neighbours, and the atoms bonded to those four.
- IRA, SOFI, and spglib reports for ice shells, hydrate cages, and
  rings are optional. The build links them when `-Dwith_ira` and
  `-Dwith_spglib` find the libraries.

### C API {#c-api}

`seams_set_num_threads(0)` restores the OpenMP width captured at first
use. That width is `omp_get_max_threads()` when OpenMP is linked, and 1
otherwise. A negative width returns `SEAMS_ERR_RANGE`.

`seams_system_set_positions` overwrites the coordinates, and optionally
the cell, of a stored frame. `seams_system_box`,
`seams_system_positions`, `seams_system_types`, and `seams_system_ids`
copy the stored frame out through a const handle.

Length-checked calls are `seams_chill_plus_n`, `seams_q4q6_n`,
`seams_rings_labels_n`, and `seams_rings_histogram_n`. The counts are
`seams_system_natoms`, `seams_neighbours_nrows`, and
`seams_rings_nrings`. `seams_last_error_message` names the last
failure. `seams_rings_chordless` lists every chordless cycle of one
size from 3 to 12, as sorted canonical rows. On 4096 mW molecules, one
thread, the six-ring census that calls it takes 3.1 ms. The census it
replaces took 20.6 ms.

Every public call returns a `seams_status`. The library does not call
`exit`.

### Packages {#packages}

Each binding is version 2.14.0.

| Language | Package | Repository |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Python | pydseamslib (import dseams and import pydseams) | PydSEAMSlib |
| Rust | crates dseams-sys and dseams | dseams-rs |
| Fortran | fpm Git dependency dseams | dseams-fortran |
| Lua, Fennel | Git source, require("dseams") | yodaStruct |
| R | package dseams | dseams-r |
| Julia | Dseams (over libseams_lang) and Seams (over libseams) | Dseams.jl |

The Meson options that built the
bindings in-tree are removed: `with_python`, `with_lua`, `fennel_lua`,
`with_fortran`, `julia_wrap`, `r_libs_user`, and `system_libseams`.

`pydseams` 2.14.0 has a Frame handle. `read`, `from_ase`, `to_ase`,
`to_solvis`, `chill_plus`, `cages`, `cages_by_signature`, `steinhardt`,
`rdf_2d`, `monolayer_rings`, `find_prisms`, and
`pydseams.band.ring_census` call `libseams_lang`. Saved trajectories
other than CON are read with chemfiles when that library is linked.
The formats include xyz, a LAMMPS dump, gro, pdb, dcd, xtc, and Amber
NetCDF.

### Engines {#engines}

LAMMPS loads `compute dseams` as `dseamsplugin.so` (`plugin load`), or
from the copy-in sources in `extras/lammps`. The plugin accepts
`cutoff`, `graph cutoff` or `graph mutual`, `rule published` or
`rule ovito`, `type I`, and `mol water`. The copy-in sources accept
`cutoff`, `graph`, `type`, and `mol`. `type` and `mol water` score
only the named oxygens. GROMACS uses a module inside `mdrun`. OpenMM
uses a reporter.

The PLUMED `SEAMS` collective variable is a separate plugin. The
standalone PLUMED action (`dseams-plumed` v0.4.1) is indexed in
[PLUMED-NEST egg 26.018](https://www.plumed-nest.org/eggs/26/018/). Meson
builds it when `-Dwith_plumed` finds PLUMED. The option defaults to
`auto`. `seams.q6` is the mean local q6, `seams.ice` is the CHILL+
cubic fraction, and `seams.ring` is the fraction of atoms on a
primitive six-ring. `MODE=all`, the default, also reports the
hexagonal count and the six-ring count. `MODE=q6` and `MODE=q6bar`
compute only the mean local q6 or the mean Lechner-Dellago q6-bar.
`DUMP=file` appends a LAMMPS dump of the coordinates handed to d-SEAMS
and the per-atom value. A restraint can bias q6. Positions are read in
PLUMED’s length unit and converted to angstroms.

### Neighbour lists and CHILL+ {#neighbour-lists-and-chill}

The cutoff list covers restricted triclinic boxes. The orthorhombic
list is a parallel cell sort. Each thread counts its atoms, a prefix
sum places them, and the pairs are written into one CSR. The pair set
does not depend on the thread count. Each OpenMP thread also owns a
block of the linkcell weighted cell cut.

On `input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj`, 250 TIP4P oxygens of LAMMPS type
2:

```bash
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2
seams chill-plus input/traj/exampleTraj.lammpstrj --cutoff 3.5 --type 2 --graph mutual
```

The cutoff command prints `nop 250 interClathrate 9 water 241`. The
mutual command prints `nop 250 clathrate 1 interClathrate 7 water 242`.

Those cutoff counts are a shell-count fix on this frame. The previous
cutoff classification reported 12 interClathrate and 238 water, because
bonds were counted after the list had been cut to four. A crystal row
needs four neighbours inside the cutoff. `seams ovito-chill+` averages
q3 on the full shell and skips that neighbour test. Plain CHILL keeps
the four closest neighbours and Moore’s test. A failure to read the
input returns exit status 2.

`--pair-types I,J` names the site-site pair for `seams rdf` and
`seams cn`. Neighbour, CHILL, CHILL+, ring, and cage calls keep water
oxygens with `--water-types` or `--mol` (`water`, or a molecule-id
list such as `1,5-12`) and leave ions out of that graph. A type or
molecule id that is absent from the frame is an error.

### Cages and symmetry {#cages-and-symmetry}

A signature cage is kept when its faces tile a sphere: every vertex
lies on at least three faces that close around it, and $V - E + F = 2$.
`--cage-edge` and `SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE` set the face-edge window, in the
coordinate units of the file. The default is `2.65,3.15`. `none` leaves
the cage bound to the face census. `Frame.cages_by_signature` and the
Lua `edge` option take the same window.

`seams rings` prints the primitive-ring census by size. Primitive rings
are the Franzblau shortest-path census. `seams prisms` counts perfect
and imperfect prisms of sizes 3 to 6.

### Performance {#performance}

On 110592-molecule ice Ic, 8 OpenMP threads run the cutoff list 4.8
times, q4 5.8 times, q6 5.9 times, and the primitive-ring census 6.1
times faster than 1 thread. The CSR, the $q_l$ values, and the ring
counts match at 1, 2, 4, and 8 threads.

When an idle 8-thread OpenMP team is already resident, 8-thread CHILL+
on that ice Ic frame takes 7 ms and the shell match takes 9 ms. The
same calls took 74 ms and 76 ms before the library narrowed its team
to the free cores. `SEAMS_FAIR_WIDTH=0` keeps the requested width.
Times on an idle machine are unchanged.

### Deprecations {#deprecations}

`--types` is a deprecated alias of `--pair-types`. Both names bind.
Using `--types` prints a one-line warning on stderr.

`seams fingerprint --color-types` is the spelling `--help` shows.
`--colour-types` remains a hidden alias of that option. A key library
writes `colors` in its header and still reads a 2.13 file that says
`colours`.

## 2.13.0 {#id2}

- Each bond row is the sorted neighbour ids.
- `seams cages` reuses a search only when the undirected edge sets
  match. Differing lists are searched on their own.
- Cage-edge windows and other decimal options parse in the C locale, so
  the same decimal text is accepted on every supported toolchain,
  including a libc++ with no floating `std::from_chars`.
- `pydseamslib` `chill_plus` takes no graph argument. The call labels
  the cutoff neighbour list.

## 2.12.0 {#id3}

Double-diamond cages are a maximum non-conflicting set.
`findDDC` builds the mutual-conflict graph once. A one-cage component
is kept. A component whose neighbourhoods are the two cliques of a
bipartite line graph is a maximum matching, certified by a König
cover. Any other component is a branch-and-bound maximum independent
set, certified by a clique partition. A degree-one candidate is kept,
and only that one conflict is dropped.

A peripheral set is kept when the seven rings span 14 molecules and
each peripheral shares exactly three atoms with the equator. When the
product of rings through the even or odd triplets exceeds 256, the
chains are built from edges that share at least three atoms, and the
lexicographically least assignment that meets the same test is kept.

On cubic mW, 4096 molecules, the certified double-diamond count is
2048, one cage for every two molecules. The search before this
certificate reported 2040. On nucleation frame 148 the double-diamond
count is 121 and the hexagonal count is 102. The search before the
certificate reported 122 double-diamond cages.

On the all-site niu2f1 frame, one thread spends 176.4 s in one run of
`findHC`, `findDDC`, and `findBySignatures` together. TRACE on that
frame spends 1762.064 s. On the mixed-site frame `findDDC` returns 0.
The search before the 14-molecule rule returned 605243 cages there,
and every hexagon of that frame fails the rule.

The clathrate face-edge window is `--cage-edge` and `SEAMS_CAGE_EDGE`,
default `2.65,3.15` in the coordinate units of the file. `none` turns
the window off.

`cages --signature` counts a face set as a cage when its faces tile a
sphere: every vertex lies on at least three faces that close around
it, and $V - E + F = 2$. Rings whose minimum-image bonds add up to a
lattice vector wind through the periodic cell and are dropped first.
On the GenIce structure I unit cell the search reports 2 $5^{12}$
cages and 6 $5^{12}6^{2}$ cages. The search before that test reported
90 $5^{12}6^{2}$, 4248 $5^{12}6^{4}$, and 218305 $5^{12}6^{8}$.

The orthorhombic cutoff list folds coordinates into the cell, bins
them one cutoff wide, and shares the 27-cell stencil across the atoms
in a cell. Interior cells skip the periodic wrap. CHILL and CHILL+ on
the default left-to-right fp64 path evaluate the $l = 3$ harmonics
as real and imaginary parts.

CHILL and CHILL+ default to the cutoff list on the command line, in
the C API, in R, in Julia, and in `compute dseams`. The mutual
four-nearest list is `--graph mutual` under that name on each of those
fronts. Those fronts used the mutual list by default before this
release.

This release adds the R package and the Julia package. Both call
`libseams_lang`.

## 2.11.0 {#id4}

- Cutoff neighbour rows and hexagonal and double-diamond cage
  affiliation run across host threads.
- Under `mpiexec`, an MPI build shares the `--frame` / `--last` range
  of a LAMMPS dump across ranks. Rank 0 prints every frame in order.
  A run without a launcher, or with `SEAMS_MPI=0`, stays on one
  process.
- Periodic distances use minimage 0.1.4. The linked-cell neighbour
  search uses linkcell 0.3.10.
- The ice XXI library matches the Lee et al. 2026 I-42d oxygen cell
  (space group $I\bar{4}2d$, Z = 152, a = b = 20.197 Å, c = 7.891 Å).
  A hit also requires a tetrahedral four-nearest graph, mean
  coordination in \[3.5, 4.5\], and a six-ring census near 112.

## 2.10.0 {#id5}

- Rodger F4 and host $q_{12}$ are per-atom fields, so the Zeron
  q3/q12 hydrate pair can be read from the command line.
- CHILL and CHILL+ default to the mutual four-nearest graph.
  `--water-types` keeps the four-neighbour list on the named water
  types, so substrate and ions stay out of it.
- Cups and incomplete cages are enumerated on the ring graph. Closed
  signature counts stay on the closed path. `seams cages --signature --incomplete` reports the open cages.
- Stacking planes of the topological unit matching (HC-basal and
  DDC-equatorial) are reported beside the CHILL+ $I_{sd}$ bins.
  `SEAMS_OFFLOAD=1` runs those hop-bound cages on a device when one is
  present, and on the host when none is. `SEAMS_OFFLOAD=0` stays on
  the host. CHILL+ itself stays on the host.
- Hexagonal channels are stacked six-ring prisms. Ice XXI (Lee et al.,
  Nat. Mater. 25, 302, 2026) also requires a tetrahedral 3.5 Å graph
  and a primitive six-ring on the Z = 152 cell.
- `compute dseams` writes per-atom CHILL+ from the C API. The example
  deck `extras/lammps/in.dseams` reads `extras/lammps/water.data` with
  `pair_style zero`.

## 2.9.2 {#id6}

Every host stage of the ring pipeline runs under OpenMP. From 2048
atoms, when OpenMP is compiled in, the cutoff neighbour list and the
index-ordered list come from `nneigh::cellListRowsThreaded`. Atoms are
binned in fractional coordinates of the recovered triclinic cell, every
axis needs three cells of perpendicular width one cutoff, and each row
is one thread’s task. The rows equal the minimum-image reference.
`neighbourListByIndex` runs one row per thread. `bench_strong` times
every host stage and their sum and keeps the best of five runs.

## 2.9.1 {#id7}

The OpenMP target offload of the Steinhardt kernel compiles with nvc++
23.7 (`-mp=gpu`) against CUDA 12.2 on an NVIDIA A100. The device path
matches the serial and threaded host paths bit for bit on the FCC
lattice and on `input/traj/mW_cubic.lammpstrj`. `SEAMS_OFFLOAD=0`
forces the host path.

## 2.9.0 {#id8}

`cage::findBySignature` enumerates closed polyhedra from a ring-size
census. `seams cages --signature` takes a census such as `4:6,6:8` or
a name (`sodalite`, `alpha`, `512`, `51262`, `hc`, `ddc`). Named `hc`
and `ddc` call `findHC` and `findDDC`, so the vertex sets match those
finders.

`topo::matchLibraries` names atoms against key libraries at several hop
counts. The deepest library that holds an atom’s key wins, and the
report includes the depth that named the atom. `seams fingerprint --library` accepts a comma-separated list.

`site::guestOccupancy` places guests in enumerated cages by the
periodic centroid of the cage vertices and counts occupied, multiply
occupied, and free cages. `--guest-types` names the guest LAMMPS types.
`site::shellRingCensus` counts, by size, the water-network rings that
pass through an ion’s shell. `--per-atom FILE` on `cages`,
`fingerprint`, and `ions` appends a LAMMPS dump frame with the engine’s
per-atom decision, for OVITO or VMD.

## 2.8.0 {#id9}

`topo::localKey` names the isomorphism class of an atom’s rooted
bonded neighbourhood. With nauty linked, the key is the nauty
certificate. Otherwise it is a Weisfeiler-Leman hash.
`topo::fingerprint` keys a frame by the sorted hashes and the primitive
ring census, so a relabelled configuration shares the key.
`--color-types` partitions keys by LAMMPS type.

`seams fingerprint --emit-library` writes a frame’s keys as library
lines. `--library` names the atoms of a later frame from that file.
`seams ions` classes ions by their first water shell against the cage
assignment. `--hops`, `--ion-types`, and `--ion-cutoff` are the new
options.

`seams cages --graph seeded --complete` turns on ring-adjacent
completion. The CLI keeps frame order for a parallel LAMMPS range,
dispatches ranges for XYZ, chemfiles, and readcon input, and writes
versioned JSONL with `--format json`. `--strict-input` makes an empty
frame an error. XYZ input accepts coordinate-only rows and records
that frame as frame 1.

CON input uses the embedded readcon reader when the engine is built
with it. CON or chemfiles input with the reader absent is refused, and
the call does not return an empty frame in its place.

## 2.7.0 {#id10}

`ring::seededCageAffiliation` takes an optional completion flag.
`ring::ringAdjacentCompletion` fills the last vertex of any six-ring
whose other vertices carry a cage label, and repeats to a fixed point.
Hexagonal-cage labels and double-diamond-cage labels are two separate
walks. The rule is stated and proved in `lean/` with Mathlib: the
completion is the least fixed point above the seed, it is empty on an
empty seed, and it does not depend on the visiting order.

## 2.6.0 {#id11}

Meson links FlexiBLAS when pkg-config or `libflexiblas` is present, and
otherwise the conda-forge `libblas` and `liblapack` packages. Python
callers use `pydseamslib` from PyPI. The nucleation notebook reads
`CageScore` fields. The Figshare Lua demos load `example_lua` from
yodaStruct.

## 2.5.0 {#id12}

`--family` selects the chemistry. The default is `waterIce`. `chill`,
`chill-plus`, `cages`, and `ions` on any other family print the family
name and return exit status 2. `seams cn --ions` is the cage degree on `site::ionCloud`. `seams pairs` counts
mutual-nearest contact pairs. `seams domains` is the largest polar or
apolar Stoddard component. `seams density-z` is the type-resolved
$\rho(z)$, with the slab volume taken from the dump cell matrix.
Running coordination numbers and the first minimum of $g_{IJ}$ come
from `rdf::runningCN` and `rdf::firstMinimumBin`. Dump writers emit
`xy`, `xz`, and `yz` when the cloud carries tilt.

## 2.4.0 {#id13}

`seams rdf` and `seams cn` compute partial three-dimensional site-site
$g_{IJ}(r)$ and coordination numbers under the dump minimum image.
Site chemistry is a `site::Table` of LAMMPS types, with optional
atom-id overrides. `site::ionCloud` collapses each ion molecule id to
one unwrapped center-of-mass vertex. Hydrogen bonds accept an explicit
donor-hydrogen index set through `populateHbondsFromDonors`. `seams hbonds --donors` treats every hydrogen as a donor candidate. The water
cutoffs on that command are the water criterion.

In-plane RDF normalization uses the dump-cell volume $|\det H|$ and
the restricted-triclinic in-plane area $l_x \times l_y$.

## 2.3.4 {#id14}

Steinhardt parameters, hydrogen bonds, and cluster wraps use the dump
minimum image.

## 2.3.3 {#id15}

Cutoff fallbacks and the skin Verlet refresh use the dump 3 by 3
minimum image.

## 2.3.2 {#id16}

Cutoff lists take the LAMMPS dump 3 by 3 cell. Device ice-score batches
pass `lammpsBoxToLinkcell` when the dump carries tilt. This release
uses linkcell v0.3.1.

## 2.3.1 {#id17}

`neighList`, `halfNeighList`, and the in-plane RDF sampler use the
vesin cell list, the same helper as `neighListO`. Brute force remains
the fallback. The GPU ice-score workspace is unchanged.

## 2.3.0 {#id18}

The topological unit-matching ice score (mutual four-nearest graph,
primitive hexagons, hexagonal and double-diamond cages) runs as a
device-resident batch of frames when gpulite and linkcell 0.3.0 are
present. CHILL and $q_{lm}$ stay on the host.

Runtime settings are read from `SEAMS_CONFIG` or from `./seams.env` in
the working directory, then from the environment, then from
command-line flags. `seams --print-config` prints the resolved table.
Examples call `seams`, `pydseams`, and `require("dseams")`. The 2020
`yodaStruct -c` and `conf.yaml` surface is removed in this release.

## 2.2.5 {#id19}

This release uses linkcell v0.2.4. A static `libyodaLib` links the static
linkcell archive, so a consumer of that archive does not need
`liblinkcell.so` at link time. Dump floating-point fields parse with
`strtod`, including on Apple libc++.

## 2.2.4 {#id20}

Periodic *k*-nearest graphs come from
[linkcell](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/linkcell) v0.2.2.
`kNearestNeighbourList` and `kNearestNeighbourPair` write packed
$n \times k$ nominations. The mutual graph and the union graph come
from one walk. The LAMMPS dump box is the bound spans plus `xy`, `xz`,
and `yz`. `periodicDistSq` recovers the cell matrix from that box. An
empty frame no longer stops the walker.

## 2.2.3 {#id21}

Help, errors, ice-type counts, and `--features` are colorized.
`NO_COLOR` turns the color off.

## 2.2.2 {#id22}

The compiled Python module in this release is `pydseams.yoda`.
`pydseams._core` remains an alias.

## 2.2.1 {#id23}

- The Nix flake packages `libyodaLib` and `seams`. The package is the
  Meson build.
- A live LAMMPS dump session, `nLammpsFrames` and
  `forEachLammpsFrame`, supports `seams --frame N --last M --jobs J`.
  Each worker opens its own handle.
- The bond graph is chosen at runtime: `cutoff`, `knn`, or
  `knn-union`. `seams cages --graph` adds `seeded`.
- LAMMPS readers bind `xu`, `yu`, `zu` and `xs`, `ys`, `zs` when `x`,
  `y`, and `z` are absent.

## 2.2.0 {#id24}

The engine command line is `seams`, with `read`, `chill`,
`chill-plus`, and `cages`. Lua callers use the `dseams` library from
yodaStruct. Python callers use `pydseams`.

## 2.1.2 {#id25}

The CMake-era Nix entry points (`default.nix`, `shell.nix`, and
`nix/yodaStruct.nix`) are removed. They still named the product
`yodaStruct`. This release builds with pixi.

## 2.1.1 {#id26}

The CHILL interfacial walk uses the same four-neighbour star as
`c_ij`. Atoms without four recorded bonds are labelled water, matching
CHILL+. Seeded affiliation floods the hexagonal cage and the
double-diamond cage as separate components, so a hexagonal seed does
not keep a double-diamond-only atom.

## 2.1.0 {#id27}

This repository is the C++ engine.

- The `yodaStruct` Lua and Fennel command line moves to
  [https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/yodaStruct) . This release rejects
  `-Dwith_lua=enabled` and names that repository. The option itself is
  removed in 2.14.0.
- Python bindings stay in
  [https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib) , where they moved in 2.0.1.
- `getCorrel`, `getCorrelPlus`, `getIceType`, `getIceTypeNoPrint`,
  `getIceTypePlus`, `getIceTypePlusNoPrint`, and `reclassifyWater`
  return `void`.

## 2.0.1 {#id28}

The Python bindings move to
[https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib](https://github.com/d-SEAMS/PydSEAMSlib) . This repository is the C++
engine. macOS wheels in this release target deployment 14, and macOS
x86_64 wheels are no longer built.

## 2.0.0 {#id30}

Meson replaces CMake. The license changes from GPL to MIT. Optional
dependencies are vesin neighbour lists, Highway SIMD, chemfiles, and
readcon-core. The engine tests are a Catch2 suite.

## 1.0.0 {#id31}

Initial release. Goswami, Goswami, and Singh, J. Chem. Inf. Model., 60, 2169-2177,
[10.1021/acs.jcim.0c00031](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.0c00031).
